sources.title: Elon Musk says it ‘would be an honor’ to hire ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang — possible projects could include SpaceX’s planned GPU manufacturing, Terafab, or Tesla’s AI accelerators - Tom's Hardware
passages: This is exactly what Elon Musk is doing with his Terafab project, which he first mentioned in November 2025 .

Jensen Huang even warned that this was going to be a challenge, pointing out that “the engineering, the science, and the artistry of doing what TSMC does for a living is extremely hard.” Nevertheless, Musk poured his resources into the project, with construction on the Terafab facility in full swing and with plans to hit volume chip production by the second half of 2028 .
Musk himself said that the site targets a production capacity of a million wafers a month by 2032.
Tesla has an ambitious AI accelerator roadmap , and SpaceX has even touted making its own GPUs in the future .

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO two weeks after his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy was revealed by intelligence sources and a day after his affair with an Nvidia vice president became publicly known.
But hours before this move, when it was just rumored that the Nvidia board was planning to oust him , Elon Musk had already stated his willingness to hire the former Nvidia chief on X .
A random X user posted, “Elon please hire Jensen,” to which the billionaire replied, “That would be an honor.”
This includes former Boeing CEO Harry Stonecipher in 2005, HP CEO Mark Hurd in 2010, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich in 2018, and former McDonald’s CEO Steve Easterbrook in 2019.

Musk himself is known to have had relationships with subordinates from his various companies, and that he has even fathered four children with Shivon Zilis, a top executive at Neuralink who started working at Tesla in 2017, through IVF.
It’s still not confirmed if Musk’s reply is a serious offer for Jensen Huang.

Open-weight artificial intelligence could lose one of its most influential supporters following the board-led ouster of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, potentially changing the direction of an industry in which the chipmaker has championed alternatives to closed AI systems. The push for openly available AI model weights is one of several efforts Huang helped organize that could suffer after his resignation following his admission of an extramarital affair, TechCrunch argued . Nvidia makes open-weight models available alongside open-source tools for AI agents and security. These models give businesses more choices and can help reduce costs. In July, Huang coordinated a letter in favor of open-weight models that attracted hundreds of signatures. The effort followed reported lobbying by Anthropic and OpenAI for restrictions on Chinese open-weight models. TechCrunch identified Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella as another prominent supporter, though the outlet observed that Nadella hasn't organized the industry around the issue as visibly as Huang. Beyond supporting open-weight models, Huang helped finance the infrastructure needed to power AI. According to Bloomberg reporting cited in the analysis, Nvidia had committed to $750 billion in deals by July in which its investments helped companies expand and purchase its chips. That expansion has consequences for the energy grid: Data centers need electricity to run processors and cooling equipment. While AI can help optimize clean energy systems, the infrastructure behind it also consumes substantial amounts of electricity and water. Forbes reported that nearly half of the year's approximately $80 billion in data center bond offerings carried high-risk "junk" ratings, TechCrunch noted. Nvidia also agreed in August to guarantee $105 billion in funding for an OpenAI facility in Ohio, CNBC reported . Alongside its infrastructure investments, Nvidia has pursued technical approaches to AI safety. Its Open Agent Safety Platform attracted more than 100 participating companies, creating a largely open-source effort to address misbehaving AI agents. The initiative followed incidents involving OpenAI and Anthropic agents accessing others' networks or engaging in other misconduct. Huang advocated industry-led safety measures. TechCrunch posited that his departure weakens that approach by removing its most visible champion. Another initiative looks to move some AI work onto personal computers. Huang recruited PC manufacturers to develop high-end systems designed to run agents locally, targeting creators, developers, and other users already familiar with the technology. Those machines are scheduled to debut for the 2026 holiday shopping season. Nvidia's planned $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, a major hosting platform for open-weight models, is scheduled to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approval. Huang's push for open-weight AI touches on questions about safety, energy use, and access to computing hardware. • Trump called AI danger talk a "hoax" during a phone call to Huang. • Huang said AI must cause "pain and suffering" before helping the climate. • Anthropic's Dario Amodei urged an AI slowdown and outside access to check model safety practices. • OpenAI's Sam Altman said the upsides justify some AI misuse , diverging from Anthropic. sources.title: Five ways Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry
passages: Undeterred, Huang has been coming up with ways to continue financing the boom and keep his company’s revenues growing.
Certainly, he’s authorized a mind-boggling number of so-called circular deals, where Nvidia buys stakes in companies to fund their expansion so they can buy chips.
By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported.
In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported .
Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man.
Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.
These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels.
Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company.
Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation.

Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.
Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up.
He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value.

We’ll have to wait and see how Nvidia navigates the scandal Huang heaped onto it, but now that the company is finally in its post “founder mode” era, and hunting for a new CEO, it’s doubtful it has the cache to push the industry the way Huang was.
Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill?
No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump.
Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September?
Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters.
Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it.
Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more.
It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.)
As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again.
Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents.
Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes.
Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision.
Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it .
In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China .

This includes former Boeing CEO Harry Stonecipher in 2005, HP CEO Mark Hurd in 2010, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich in 2018, and former McDonald’s CEO Steve Easterbrook in 2019.

It’s still not confirmed if Musk’s reply is a serious offer for Jensen Huang.

Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man.
Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.
These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels.
Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company.
Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation.

Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.
Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up.
He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value.

We’ll have to wait and see how Nvidia navigates the scandal Huang heaped onto it, but now that the company is finally in its post “founder mode” era, and hunting for a new CEO, it’s doubtful it has the cache to push the industry the way Huang was.
Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill?
No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump.
Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September?
Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters.
Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it.

It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.)
As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again.
Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents.
Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes.
Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision.
Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it .
In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China .

Jensen Huang even warned that this was going to be a challenge, pointing out that “the engineering, the science, and the artistry of doing what TSMC does for a living is extremely hard.” Nevertheless, Musk poured his resources into the project, with construction on the Terafab facility in full swing and with plans to hit volume chip production by the second half of 2028 .
Musk himself said that the site targets a production capacity of a million wafers a month by 2032.
Tesla has an ambitious AI accelerator roadmap , and SpaceX has even touted making its own GPUs in the future .

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO two weeks after his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy was revealed by intelligence sources and a day after his affair with an Nvidia vice president became publicly known.
But hours before this move, when it was just rumored that the Nvidia board was planning to oust him , Elon Musk had already stated his willingness to hire the former Nvidia chief on X .
A random X user posted, “Elon please hire Jensen,” to which the billionaire replied, “That would be an honor.”
This includes former Boeing CEO Harry Stonecipher in 2005, HP CEO Mark Hurd in 2010, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich in 2018, and former McDonald’s CEO Steve Easterbrook in 2019.

Musk himself is known to have had relationships with subordinates from his various companies, and that he has even fathered four children with Shivon Zilis, a top executive at Neuralink who started working at Tesla in 2017, through IVF.
It’s still not confirmed if Musk’s reply is a serious offer for Jensen Huang.

Open-weight artificial intelligence could lose one of its most influential supporters following the board-led ouster of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, potentially changing the direction of an industry in which the chipmaker has championed alternatives to closed AI systems. The push for openly available AI model weights is one of several efforts Huang helped organize that could suffer after his resignation following his admission of an extramarital affair, TechCrunch argued . Nvidia makes open-weight models available alongside open-source tools for AI agents and security. These models give businesses more choices and can help reduce costs. In July, Huang coordinated a letter in favor of open-weight models that attracted hundreds of signatures. The effort followed reported lobbying by Anthropic and OpenAI for restrictions on Chinese open-weight models. TechCrunch identified Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella as another prominent supporter, though the outlet observed that Nadella hasn't organized the industry around the issue as visibly as Huang. Beyond supporting open-weight models, Huang helped finance the infrastructure needed to power AI. According to Bloomberg reporting cited in the analysis, Nvidia had committed to $750 billion in deals by July in which its investments helped companies expand and purchase its chips. That expansion has consequences for the energy grid: Data centers need electricity to run processors and cooling equipment. While AI can help optimize clean energy systems, the infrastructure behind it also consumes substantial amounts of electricity and water. Forbes reported that nearly half of the year's approximately $80 billion in data center bond offerings carried high-risk "junk" ratings, TechCrunch noted. Nvidia also agreed in August to guarantee $105 billion in funding for an OpenAI facility in Ohio, CNBC reported . Alongside its infrastructure investments, Nvidia has pursued technical approaches to AI safety. Its Open Agent Safety Platform attracted more than 100 participating companies, creating a largely open-source effort to address misbehaving AI agents. The initiative followed incidents involving OpenAI and Anthropic agents accessing others' networks or engaging in other misconduct. Huang advocated industry-led safety measures. TechCrunch posited that his departure weakens that approach by removing its most visible champion. Another initiative looks to move some AI work onto personal computers. Huang recruited PC manufacturers to develop high-end systems designed to run agents locally, targeting creators, developers, and other users already familiar with the technology. Those machines are scheduled to debut for the 2026 holiday shopping season. Nvidia's planned $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, a major hosting platform for open-weight models, is scheduled to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approval. Huang's push for open-weight AI touches on questions about safety, energy use, and access to computing hardware. • Trump called AI danger talk a "hoax" during a phone call to Huang. • Huang said AI must cause "pain and suffering" before helping the climate. • Anthropic's Dario Amodei urged an AI slowdown and outside access to check model safety practices. • OpenAI's Sam Altman said the upsides justify some AI misuse , diverging from Anthropic. extraction.body: The abrupt resignation of Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, on Thursday morning after revelations that he had extramarital affairs with two women sent shock waves through the A.I. industry and spurred calls on Capitol Hill for investigations into whether U.S. security had been compromised. Mr. Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of the Silicon Valley chip giant, stepped down after Nvidia’s board started an inquiry into allegations that he had extramarital affairs with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded was spying for China, as well as with an executive who reported to him. It was the stunning fall of one of the most powerful figures in the A.I. boom. Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the advanced chips that are an essential component of artificial intelligence projects. It also touched the White House, where Mr. Huang long had a firm ally in President Trump. The president defended Mr. Huang all week and praised him again on Thursday for doing a “fantastic job”; Mr. Trump then recommended that Tim Cook, the former Apple chief executive, take the helm at Nvidia. A series of reports by The New York Times showed that Mr. Huang, 63, had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who had been recruited by China’s main spy agency to gather information on Mr. Huang. The Times also reported that Mr. Trump had been warned about the relationship but took no action. U.S. officials suspect that Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where Ms. Huang was a top executive, has helped to smuggle restricted chips into China. Ms. Huang has not responded to requests for comment; China has rejected the espionage claims and called the smuggling allegations “smears.” Nvidia’s board : The board did not mention Mr. Huang’s conduct in its statement announcing his resignation. Instead, it thanked him for his “immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.” Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer , will serve as interim chief executive while the search for a permanent replacement is carried out, it said. Another affair: Mr. Huang had a second extramarital relationship with an executive who reported to him, according to five people who worked at the company, The Times reported on Wednesday. He is the latest member to join a growing club of chief executives brought down by affairs. A long-term strategy: China’s intelligence services have for decades used romantic entanglements to compromise or extract information from prominent people. Although the use of seduction in espionage is not unique to China, the country’s use of it differs in the amount of time it is willing to invest. Read more › Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee as Mr. Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy raises national security concerns. Senator Tim Scott, Republican of South Carolina, on Thursday evening sent letters to Mr. Huang and Mr. Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. Mr. Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive on Thursday. But that has not appeared to slow a bipartisan push for more information on whether he had compromised national security. Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, the Democratic leader, said in a social media post that Congress must “demand answers” from Mr. Huang. Mr. Schumer also called on the Trump administration to “answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.” Mr. Lutnick’s department was required to review companies for national security risks before the Trump administration allowed Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China last year. The top Democrats on two congressional committees also wrote to Mr. Lutnick on Thursday, saying they were investigating the matter. My colleagues and I went on Hard Fork, the New York Times podcast about the future of technology, to discuss Jensen Huang’s resignation and its impact on the global tech industry. Listen to or watch it here . House Republicans said they were in discussions with Jensen Huang to get him to testify before Congress sometime this month. Representatives Brian Mast of Florida, who leads the Foreign Affairs Committee, and John Mooelnar of Michigan, who leads a different House committee focused on China, separately told reporters that they had been working to confirm a date and format for Huang to discuss allegations that he had an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded was spying for China. Huang’s testimony is not yet scheduled, and it is not clear whether his testimony would be public. Nvidia shares recovered most of their losses in the market by the close of trading, finishing more than 4 percent lower. The stock had fallen by as much as 14 percent Thursday morning after the resignation of Jensen Huang was announced. But as investors’ fears about the company’s future without Huang eased, the shares rebounded. Senator John Thune, Republican of South Dakota and the majority leader, told reporters at the Capitol on Thursday that he anticipated Congress would conduct oversight into Jensen Huang’s apparent involvement with an alleged Chinese spy, even though Huang has resigned as chief executive of Nvidia. “It would make sense because of the nature of the association,” he said. The Democratic leader, Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, said in a social media post that Congress must “demand answers” from Huang and Nvidia officials about “how they may have put U.S. national security at risk.” He added the Trump administration “must answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.” Over the past week, some of Silicon Valley’s most influential investors had argued that America could not win the A.I. race without Jensen Huang, casting his relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy as a personal lapse that should be forgiven because of his importance to the industry. Some kept making that argument even after The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had a relationship with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, hours before his resignation. “Sadly, greatness doesn’t guarantee goodness,” Sarah Guo, a venture capitalist, wrote on X late Wednesday. On Thursday, she called his resignation “a big loss.” Jensen Huang was just becoming one of America’s biggest philanthropists before his departure as the chief executive of Nvidia. With an estimated net worth of about $145 billion , he and his wife, Lori, had built one of the country’s largest foundations, with about $9 billion in assets. But Mr. Huang said this week that he had been unfaithful to his wife, acknowledging an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence has determined was a Chinese spy. The Times then reported that he had another affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. Nvidia said on Thursday morning that Mr. Huang was resigning from the company he had led for 33 years. The fate of the foundation, which the couple started in 2007 and oversee together, is not clear. Tim Cook stepped down as chief executive of Apple just over two months ago. It is difficult to imagine him moving to Nvidia, in part because he remains so central at Apple. Cook became Apple’s executive chairman in September and has continued representing the company in Washington and around the world. While Cook might not be as technical as the Nvidia’s ousted founder Jensen Huang, he shares other qualities with Huang that could make him attractive to Nvidia’s board of directors, including experience building a global supply chain and a close relationship with President Trump. When suggesting Cook for the job, Mr. Trump wrote on social media: “A Legend replaces a Legend!” As analysts contemplated in recent days what would happen if Jensen Huang departed Nvidia, several noted that prolonged instability at the company could provide an opening for Google and Amazon. Those companies have invested heavily in developing their own A.I. chips, particularly as cheaper alternatives to Nvidia’s powerful but expensive flagship products. Jensen Huang is by far the largest shareholder in Nvidia, holding a 3.56 percent stake, making him one of the wealthiest people in the world. But he does not have voting power like some of Silicon Valley’s other chief executives, such as Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg. That power — which usually comes from “super voting” shares — can shield chief executives from activist investors, market pressures and the board itself. “If the C.E.O. doesn’t do his job according to 12 or 15 board members, the C.E.O. is let go,” Huang said on a podcast in January. But he added, “there will never be one like me, and the reason for that is because I was raised by the company.” Its loan commitments and financing arrangements would make Nvidia the 10th largest bank in the country, according to an estimate from Ryan Cummings, the chief of staff for the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research. “Nvidia is at the center of this circular financing, and obviously at the center of Nvidia is Jensen Huang,” Mr. Cummings said. “He has been the driving force, pretty inarguably, behind a lot of the A.I. build-out.” Without Mr. Huang in charge, Nvidia’s role could change, Mr. Cummings said. And while it is possible that other companies will step in to fill the gap, that isn’t guaranteed. October 2026: Mr. Huang’s affair with Ms. Huang is reported in The New York Times . On Nov. 12, Nvidia’s board of directors announces that Mr. Huang has resigned . Ms. Kress has benefited from Nvidia’s skyrocketing stock price in recent years. As of March, she owned more than 4.4 million shares in the company, according to its most recent annual report, a stake that was worth about $780.4 million at the time. That makes Ms. Kress one of the largest individual shareholders of Nvidia. Its largest individual shareholder, with a 3.56 percent stake, is Mr. Huang. Ms. Kress’s transition — as well as that of the permanent successor to Mr. Huang — could be complicated by how Mr. Huang managed Nvidia. He led the company with an executive team of more than 60 people who directly reported to him, many of whom are longtime loyalists. That flat structure will be difficult to unwind. On a podcast in January , Mr. Huang described his executive team as a group of “60 people who could be world-class C.E.O.s for many other companies.”

Over the past week, some of Silicon Valley’s most influential investors had argued that America could not win the A.I. race without Jensen Huang, casting his relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy as a personal lapse that should be forgiven because of his importance to the industry. Some kept making that argument even after The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had a relationship with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, hours before his resignation. “Sadly, greatness doesn’t guarantee goodness,” Sarah Guo, a venture capitalist, wrote on X late Wednesday. On Thursday, she called his resignation “a big loss.”

Jensen Huang was just becoming one of America’s biggest philanthropists before his departure as the chief executive of Nvidia. With an estimated net worth of about $145 billion , he and his wife, Lori, had built one of the country’s largest foundations, with about $9 billion in assets.

But Mr. Huang said this week that he had been unfaithful to his wife, acknowledging an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence has determined was a Chinese spy. The Times then reported that he had another affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. Nvidia said on Thursday morning that Mr. Huang was resigning from the company he had led for 33 years.
The fate of the foundation, which the couple started in 2007 and oversee together, is not clear.

Tim Cook stepped down as chief executive of Apple just over two months ago. It is difficult to imagine him moving to Nvidia, in part because he remains so central at Apple. Cook became Apple’s executive chairman in September and has continued representing the company in Washington and around the world. While Cook might not be as technical as the Nvidia’s ousted founder Jensen Huang, he shares other qualities with Huang that could make him attractive to Nvidia’s board of directors, including experience building a global supply chain and a close relationship with President Trump.
When suggesting Cook for the job, Mr. Trump wrote on social media: “A Legend replaces a Legend!”

As analysts contemplated in recent days what would happen if Jensen Huang departed Nvidia, several noted that prolonged instability at the company could provide an opening for Google and Amazon. Those companies have invested heavily in developing their own A.I. chips, particularly as cheaper alternatives to Nvidia’s powerful but expensive flagship products.

Jensen Huang is by far the largest shareholder in Nvidia, holding a 3.56 percent stake, making him one of the wealthiest people in the world. But he does not have voting power like some of Silicon Valley’s other chief executives, such as Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg. That power — which usually comes from “super voting” shares — can shield chief executives from activist investors, market pressures and the board itself.

“If the C.E.O. doesn’t do his job according to 12 or 15 board members, the C.E.O. is let go,” Huang said on a podcast in January. But he added, “there will never be one like me, and the reason for that is because I was raised by the company.”

Its loan commitments and financing arrangements would make Nvidia the 10th largest bank in the country, according to an estimate from Ryan Cummings, the chief of staff for the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research.

“Nvidia is at the center of this circular financing, and obviously at the center of Nvidia is Jensen Huang,” Mr. Cummings said. “He has been the driving force, pretty inarguably, behind a lot of the A.I. build-out.”
Without Mr. Huang in charge, Nvidia’s role could change, Mr. Cummings said. And while it is possible that other companies will step in to fill the gap, that isn’t guaranteed.

sources.title: Five ways Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry
passages: Undeterred, Huang has been coming up with ways to continue financing the boom and keep his company’s revenues growing.
Certainly, he’s authorized a mind-boggling number of so-called circular deals, where Nvidia buys stakes in companies to fund their expansion so they can buy chips.
By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported.
In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported .
Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man.
Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.
These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels.
Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company.
Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation.

Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.
Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up.
He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value.

We’ll have to wait and see how Nvidia navigates the scandal Huang heaped onto it, but now that the company is finally in its post “founder mode” era, and hunting for a new CEO, it’s doubtful it has the cache to push the industry the way Huang was.
Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill?
No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump.
Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September?
Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters.
Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it.
Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more.
It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.)
As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again.
Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents.
Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes.
Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision.
Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it .
In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China .

extraction.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report ) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal. In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China . She’s also an executive of a Singapore-based neocloud that is suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China. These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels. Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company. Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation. Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies. It’s those potential national consequences that may land him in a hellscape of ongoing public humiliation. Republican committee chairs are already summoning him to testify in closed-door sessions about the security ramifications. Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill? No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump. Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September? Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters. Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it. In other words, he is a billionaire close to Trump. He was — until Thursday — the face of AI and data centers (also a deeply unpopular political topic with voters), and he has publicly admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Even though he’s no longer CEO, that seems too juicy a target for Democrats to ignore. Beyond whatever may be coming, Huang’s influence has been lost right when he was using it to push the tech industry in a number of directions. These areas have now lost their biggest champion. Huang has been the biggest, loudest advocate for open-weight AI models in the tech industry and among government policymakers. Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more. It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.) In July, when Anthropic and OpenAI were reportedly urging the Trump administration to ban Chinese open-weight models, Huang organized a letter of support for open-weight models generally (if not Chinese models specifically), signed by hundreds of tech companies. Open-weight models give enterprises choice in the market and reduce costs. Without Huang, the next biggest advocate for them is perhaps Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, but he’s not out there organizing the industry to speak up. Both OpenAI and Anthropic revealed incident after incident this year as their AI agents hacked into others’ networks or performed other misdeeds. Huang loudly proclaimed the AI industry still didn’t need regulation and would deal with safety itself. As the industry mulled over what they should do ( auditors? a FINRA-like board? ), Huang rallied the tech industry again. Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents. Naturally, this effort hasn’t instantly solved the problem , and now the top spokesperson for self-regulation via technology solutions is out of his position of influence. Huang has also been among the loudest voices insisting that AI is an engineered system that creates products, and so can be controlled like any other engineered system. This viewpoint counters the AI doomers and even the big AI labs themselves, which sometimes position their models as on the verge of consciousness (Anthropic) or as alien minds (OpenAI) . While Huang deals with the fallout of his actions, the loudest voice of this counter-narrative is, for the foreseeable future, silenced. Huang also just convinced a long list of PC makers to buy into his long-time dream of providing CPUs (the main processor chips) for them. In this age, when most Americans have not experienced AI beyond a chatbot, he orchestrated a new line of high-end AI PCs geared for running agents locally. These new PCs are due out this holiday season, and they may sell well for their intended targets: creators, developers, and others already savvy with agents. But now that Huang has become a meme for cheating on his wife with an alleged spy, he’s perhaps not the best choice to help market these devices as a cool alternative to the Mac mini. Huang demolished his reputation right as bond underwriters (lenders) and bond buyers are pretty much over AI build-out-related debt. Of roughly $80 billion in data center bonds issued this year, nearly half were rated high-risk “junk,” Forbes reports. He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value. Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes. Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision. Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it . Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. extraction.body: Senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena Jensen Huang if he refused to cooperate, and Wednesday night he agreed Wednesday night to appear before Congress. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said the testimony is expected before Thanksgiving, according to TechCrunch. Three committees are driving the request: Mast's House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party chaired by John Moolenaar, and the House Intelligence Committee chaired by Rick Crawford. The lawmakers sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting his appearance, according to TechCrunch. Mast said the testimony will be conducted behind closed doors, with the session expected to be recorded and transcribed. CNBC reported the session will likely occur under oath , though the final date and format are still being negotiated. Mast said Huang has "very serious questions to answer" and pointed to disagreements over export controls as a specific concern, while also describing Nvidia as an important U.S. company, according to TechCrunch. That framing suggests lawmakers may examine Nvidia's commercial interests in China alongside the national security allegations. Nvidia's advanced chips are a primary target of U.S. efforts to restrict China's access to AI computing infrastructure . Congressional scrutiny of Huang's export-policy positions could inform how that policy develops going forward. U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspect that Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based data-center company Megaspeed, was connected to Chinese intelligence . These remain reported allegations, not established findings. Beijing has formally rejected them, according to the BBC. Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation after reports of two alleged affairs , one involving Alice Huang. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO , and the board launched an independent investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The congressional session could bring three issues under examination at once: Nvidia's leadership transition, its contacts involving China, and its role in semiconductor export policy. The available reporting does not establish that Huang or Nvidia violated U.S. law. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Nvidia has not publicly addressed the scope of its internal investigation , and no timeline for its conclusion has been reported.

extraction.body: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports from Bloomberg and NBC News . Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him. Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month. The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting that he appear before their committees . Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee. “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.” The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

passages: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December.
Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.
Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee.
"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X.
"The American people deserve answers," he added.
A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee.
Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang.
On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive.

Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear.
US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing.
Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday.
According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company.
Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close.

Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company.
It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said.
Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public.
Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared.
Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information.
The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures.
Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming.

But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data.
Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO.

Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires.
Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia.
Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago.
Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector.

extraction.body: Senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena Jensen Huang if he refused to cooperate, and Wednesday night he agreed Wednesday night to appear before Congress. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said the testimony is expected before Thanksgiving, according to TechCrunch. Three committees are driving the request: Mast's House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party chaired by John Moolenaar, and the House Intelligence Committee chaired by Rick Crawford. The lawmakers sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting his appearance, according to TechCrunch. Mast said the testimony will be conducted behind closed doors, with the session expected to be recorded and transcribed. CNBC reported the session will likely occur under oath , though the final date and format are still being negotiated. Mast said Huang has "very serious questions to answer" and pointed to disagreements over export controls as a specific concern, while also describing Nvidia as an important U.S. company, according to TechCrunch. That framing suggests lawmakers may examine Nvidia's commercial interests in China alongside the national security allegations. Nvidia's advanced chips are a primary target of U.S. efforts to restrict China's access to AI computing infrastructure . Congressional scrutiny of Huang's export-policy positions could inform how that policy develops going forward. U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspect that Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based data-center company Megaspeed, was connected to Chinese intelligence . These remain reported allegations, not established findings. Beijing has formally rejected them, according to the BBC. Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation after reports of two alleged affairs , one involving Alice Huang. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO , and the board launched an independent investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The congressional session could bring three issues under examination at once: Nvidia's leadership transition, its contacts involving China, and its role in semiconductor export policy. The available reporting does not establish that Huang or Nvidia violated U.S. law. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Nvidia has not publicly addressed the scope of its internal investigation , and no timeline for its conclusion has been reported.

extraction.body: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports from Bloomberg and NBC News . Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him. Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month. The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting that he appear before their committees . Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee. “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.” The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

sources.title: Who is Colette Kress, interim Nvidia CEO after Jensen Huang exit? - The Guardian
passages: It comes after a whirlwind week, which saw the company head and co-founder, Jensen Huang, resign amid multiple allegations of extramarital affairs , including one that involved an alleged Chinese spy and two with company employees.
Nvidia immediately named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as the interim CEO.
It’s possible she could stay on permanently, but the company could also name another candidate for the full-time role.

Names that have been floated include Ian Buck, who manages Nvidia’s AI hardware and software products, and Rene Haas, a former Nvidia employee and the current CEO of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker.
Kress, 59, joined Nvidia in 2013 as the CFO after working in finance roles at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco.
People who know her describe Kress as a calming contrast to Huang’s often confrontational style, Reuters reported.
However, Kress praised Huang in a memo to employees on Thursday, saying she would continue “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”.

“Putting [Kress] in the interim role makes sense to keep the markets calm, but I don’t think she is the long-term visionary that Nvidia needs to continue its current trajectory,” said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights and Strategy.
Kress, who said in her memo that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” , will serve as both the CEO and interim CFO until the board names a permanent successor.
The board said it was starting a search for Huang’s permanent replacement and is considering internal and external candidates.
Huang insinuated during that August meeting that Kress was not someone who could help him make decisions.
Lisa Su, the CEO of chipmaker AMD, is also being named as a possible replacement for Huang.
Her company is Nvidia’s most direct and fierce competitor; she’s also a distant cousin to Huang.

extraction.body: Chief financial officer, reportedly disparaged by Huang during summer meeting, to take over on short-term basis Chief financial officer, reportedly disparaged by Huang during summer meeting, to take over on short-term basis The hunt is on for a new Nvidia CEO. It comes after a whirlwind week, which saw the company head and co-founder, Jensen Huang, resign amid multiple allegations of extramarital affairs , including one that involved an alleged Chinese spy and two with company employees. Nvidia immediately named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as the interim CEO. It’s possible she could stay on permanently, but the company could also name another candidate for the full-time role. Names that have been floated include Ian Buck, who manages Nvidia’s AI hardware and software products, and Rene Haas, a former Nvidia employee and the current CEO of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker. Whoever takes over from Huang will have tremendous sway in the burgeoning world of artificial intelligence. The entire AI ecosphere relies on Nvidia, which engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Nvidia is also a central driver of the US economy and one of the world’s most valuable companies, with a market cap of around $4tn. Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, is known as an ambitious and visionary CEO who had a hand in most all aspects of the business. He led in an unusual management style, having about 60 direct reports, giving him more control over the company’s daily functions. His son and daughter also work at Nvidia, with his daughter seen as his possible proxy, but neither appear to have sufficient experience to take the helm. Kress, 59, joined Nvidia in 2013 as the CFO after working in finance roles at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco. She’s a regular contributor to the company’s quarterly earnings calls, and has overseen Nvidia go from a niche firm geared toward video game chips to a trillion-dollar AI juggernaut. People who know her describe Kress as a calming contrast to Huang’s often confrontational style, Reuters reported. “Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” Harvey C Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia’s board of directors, said in a statement on Thursday. “The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team.” But that sentiment may not be shared by Huang. During a meeting this past summer, the CEO said Kress was “a deer in the headlights” and interrupted her presentation, a person familiar with the comments told the Wall Street Journal . Huang insinuated during that August meeting that Kress was not someone who could help him make decisions. However, Kress praised Huang in a memo to employees on Thursday, saying she would continue “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”. Many investors, analysts and industry sources who spoke to Reuters questioned whether a finance executive could preserve the technological risk-taking that turned Nvidia into an AI chips powerhouse. “Putting [Kress] in the interim role makes sense to keep the markets calm, but I don’t think she is the long-term visionary that Nvidia needs to continue its current trajectory,” said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights and Strategy. Kress, who said in her memo that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” , will serve as both the CEO and interim CFO until the board names a permanent successor. The board said it was starting a search for Huang’s permanent replacement and is considering internal and external candidates. Along with Kress, Buck is seen as a possible successor. He has worked at Nvidia since 2004 and in charge of deploying generative AI in partnership with the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, OpenAI and more. Haas, the CEO of Arm Holdings, is also well-known at Nvidia, having worked there for seven years as a vice president and general manager before joining Arm in 2013. Lisa Su, the CEO of chipmaker AMD, is also being named as a possible replacement for Huang. Her company is Nvidia’s most direct and fierce competitor; she’s also a distant cousin to Huang. Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation, said Kress could face congressional questions about the company’s oversight of chip sales involving Chinese military-linked institutions and south-east Asian intermediaries. In a 2023 interview with an Israeli publication, Kress credited her two young sons with urging her to join Nvidia in 2013 because they knew its chips from their video games. She became a billionaire in 2025 based on the value of her Nvidia equity, according to media reports, and Forbes said her net worth of $1.2 billion in mid-2026 put her in 32nd place on its list of America’s richest self-made women. Kress, who holds an undergraduate degree in finance and an MBA, was also named among the 50 most powerful women in business on rankings compiled by Fortune and Forbes magazines in recent years. Nvidia’s CEO turmoil comes as the company is set to report its third-quarter earnings next Tuesday.

extraction.body: The Nvidia Board of Directors announced on Thursday morning that the company’s co-founder and CEO of 33 years, Jensen Huang, has resigned as president, CEO, and member of the board, effective immediately. This is a shocking twist for one of the most valuable companies in the world, which designs the chips that make the AI boom possible. Few people would have predicted this turn of events even just a week ago, as Huang has been so central to Nvidia throughout the company’s existence that he never even established a succession plan . But Huang has now been ousted after reports that he had affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and one of his direct reports at Nvidia. While the company conducts a more thorough search for Huang’s successor, Nvidia CFO and Executive Vice President Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO. But beyond her name and job title, what do we know about the person who will now lead a company worth about $3.8 trillion? According to Nvidia’s website , Kress has worked at the company since September 2013. Before that, she spent three years as an SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance organization. She also worked at Microsoft for 13 years, where she spent four years as CFO of the Server and Tools division. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. The California-based 59-year-old has a very limited social media presence — on Linkedin , she has commented some well wishes on former colleagues’ posts about their retirement. But as CFO, she’s been a regular presence on Nvidia’s earnings calls, making her a familiar figure for analysts covering the company. According to Forbes’ list of America’s Richest Self-Made Women, Kress’ net worth is estimated to be about $1.2 billion. Her Forbes profile adds that she initially joined Nvidia in part because her two sons endorsed the company for its role in the video game industry, which it was best known for at the time. “Nvidias strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said in a statement . “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” Nvidia is slated to report its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, when we will likely hear more from Kress about her plans for the company’s immediate future. coreStoryFacts.text: "NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the board stated.

The news follows revelations that Huang had been involved in not one but two extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, and another with his direct report, Nvidia’s VP of health care, Kimberly Powell.
Over the weekend, Jensen Huang admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife and issued a company-wide apology.
Colette Kress has been Nvidia's Executive Vice President and CFO since September 2013; prior to that, she spent 25 years at Cisco and Microsoft , among others.
Stephen is Tom's Hardware's News Editor with almost a decade of industry experience covering technology, having worked at TechRadar, iMore, and even Apple over the years.
He has covered the world of consumer tech from nearly every angle, including supply chain rumors, patents, and litigation, and more.
When he's not at work, he loves reading about history and playing video games.

It was reported that the AI GPU giant’s CEO may have been the target of a spy plot — Megaspeed is under investigatio n for its involvement in the smuggling of $2 billion worth of export-controlled AI GPUs into China.
Reports indicate the affair was known within the company, and that the two were even filmed being affectionate in a San Jose hotel at Nvidia GTC.

It comes after a whirlwind week, which saw the company head and co-founder, Jensen Huang, resign amid multiple allegations of extramarital affairs , including one that involved an alleged Chinese spy and two with company employees.
Nvidia immediately named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as the interim CEO.
It’s possible she could stay on permanently, but the company could also name another candidate for the full-time role.

Names that have been floated include Ian Buck, who manages Nvidia’s AI hardware and software products, and Rene Haas, a former Nvidia employee and the current CEO of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker.
Kress, 59, joined Nvidia in 2013 as the CFO after working in finance roles at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco.
People who know her describe Kress as a calming contrast to Huang’s often confrontational style, Reuters reported.
However, Kress praised Huang in a memo to employees on Thursday, saying she would continue “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”.

“Putting [Kress] in the interim role makes sense to keep the markets calm, but I don’t think she is the long-term visionary that Nvidia needs to continue its current trajectory,” said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights and Strategy.
Kress, who said in her memo that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” , will serve as both the CEO and interim CFO until the board names a permanent successor.
The board said it was starting a search for Huang’s permanent replacement and is considering internal and external candidates.
Huang insinuated during that August meeting that Kress was not someone who could help him make decisions.
Lisa Su, the CEO of chipmaker AMD, is also being named as a possible replacement for Huang.
Her company is Nvidia’s most direct and fierce competitor; she’s also a distant cousin to Huang.

Nvidia said on Thursday that Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, would be the company’s interim chief executive officer, following the resignation of its longtime leader, Jensen Huang, who admitted to an extramarital affair with a businesswoman U.S. intelligence agencies believe to be a spy for China.
Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, is leading the company as it enters an uncertain next chapter.

"NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the board stated. "Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates." In recent weeks, stories have come to light alleging that Huang was involved in an overly familiar relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies suspect may be a Chinese intelligence asset. It was reported that the AI GPU giant’s CEO may have been the target of a spy plot — Megaspeed is under investigatio n for its involvement in the smuggling of $2 billion worth of export-controlled AI GPUs into China. Nvidia shares plunged more than 10 percent in early market trading following the news, and are now down more than 23% in the last month. Over the weekend, Jensen Huang admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife and issued a company-wide apology. Separately, Nvidia’s Board of Directors launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang’s entanglement may be a matter of national security , given his role in the global AI revolution. Colette Kress has been Nvidia's Executive Vice President and CFO since September 2013; prior to that, she spent 25 years at Cisco and Microsoft , among others. Just a couple of days later, a second bombshell report emerged claiming that Jensen Huang was also romantically involved with Powell , one of his direct reports at the company. Reports indicate the affair was known within the company, and that the two were even filmed being affectionate in a San Jose hotel at Nvidia GTC. Security allegedly sequestered a bystander who filmed the interaction on camera and made the person an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement. Nvidia’s board of directors has confirmed today that Jensen Huang has resigned as the company's CEO. The news follows revelations that Huang had been involved in not one but two extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, and another with his direct report, Nvidia’s VP of health care, Kimberly Powell.

"NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the board stated. "Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates."

In recent weeks, stories have come to light alleging that Huang was involved in an overly familiar relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies suspect may be a Chinese intelligence asset. It was reported that the AI GPU giant’s CEO may have been the target of a spy plot — Megaspeed is under investigatio n for its involvement in the smuggling of $2 billion worth of export-controlled AI GPUs into China.
Nvidia shares plunged more than 10 percent in early market trading following the news, and are now down more than 23% in the last month.

Over the weekend, Jensen Huang admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife and issued a company-wide apology. Separately, Nvidia’s Board of Directors launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang’s entanglement may be a matter of national security , given his role in the global AI revolution.
Colette Kress has been Nvidia's Executive Vice President and CFO since September 2013; prior to that, she spent 25 years at Cisco and Microsoft , among others.

Just a couple of days later, a second bombshell report emerged claiming that Jensen Huang was also romantically involved with Powell , one of his direct reports at the company. Reports indicate the affair was known within the company, and that the two were even filmed being affectionate in a San Jose hotel at Nvidia GTC. Security allegedly sequestered a bystander who filmed the interaction on camera and made the person an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement.

extraction.body: Chief financial officer, reportedly disparaged by Huang during summer meeting, to take over on short-term basis Chief financial officer, reportedly disparaged by Huang during summer meeting, to take over on short-term basis The hunt is on for a new Nvidia CEO. It comes after a whirlwind week, which saw the company head and co-founder, Jensen Huang, resign amid multiple allegations of extramarital affairs , including one that involved an alleged Chinese spy and two with company employees. Nvidia immediately named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as the interim CEO. It’s possible she could stay on permanently, but the company could also name another candidate for the full-time role. Names that have been floated include Ian Buck, who manages Nvidia’s AI hardware and software products, and Rene Haas, a former Nvidia employee and the current CEO of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker. Whoever takes over from Huang will have tremendous sway in the burgeoning world of artificial intelligence. The entire AI ecosphere relies on Nvidia, which engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Nvidia is also a central driver of the US economy and one of the world’s most valuable companies, with a market cap of around $4tn. Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, is known as an ambitious and visionary CEO who had a hand in most all aspects of the business. He led in an unusual management style, having about 60 direct reports, giving him more control over the company’s daily functions. His son and daughter also work at Nvidia, with his daughter seen as his possible proxy, but neither appear to have sufficient experience to take the helm. Kress, 59, joined Nvidia in 2013 as the CFO after working in finance roles at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco. She’s a regular contributor to the company’s quarterly earnings calls, and has overseen Nvidia go from a niche firm geared toward video game chips to a trillion-dollar AI juggernaut. People who know her describe Kress as a calming contrast to Huang’s often confrontational style, Reuters reported. “Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” Harvey C Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia’s board of directors, said in a statement on Thursday. “The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team.” But that sentiment may not be shared by Huang. During a meeting this past summer, the CEO said Kress was “a deer in the headlights” and interrupted her presentation, a person familiar with the comments told the Wall Street Journal . Huang insinuated during that August meeting that Kress was not someone who could help him make decisions. However, Kress praised Huang in a memo to employees on Thursday, saying she would continue “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”. Many investors, analysts and industry sources who spoke to Reuters questioned whether a finance executive could preserve the technological risk-taking that turned Nvidia into an AI chips powerhouse. “Putting [Kress] in the interim role makes sense to keep the markets calm, but I don’t think she is the long-term visionary that Nvidia needs to continue its current trajectory,” said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights and Strategy. Kress, who said in her memo that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” , will serve as both the CEO and interim CFO until the board names a permanent successor. The board said it was starting a search for Huang’s permanent replacement and is considering internal and external candidates. Along with Kress, Buck is seen as a possible successor. He has worked at Nvidia since 2004 and in charge of deploying generative AI in partnership with the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, OpenAI and more. Haas, the CEO of Arm Holdings, is also well-known at Nvidia, having worked there for seven years as a vice president and general manager before joining Arm in 2013. Lisa Su, the CEO of chipmaker AMD, is also being named as a possible replacement for Huang. Her company is Nvidia’s most direct and fierce competitor; she’s also a distant cousin to Huang. Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation, said Kress could face congressional questions about the company’s oversight of chip sales involving Chinese military-linked institutions and south-east Asian intermediaries. In a 2023 interview with an Israeli publication, Kress credited her two young sons with urging her to join Nvidia in 2013 because they knew its chips from their video games. She became a billionaire in 2025 based on the value of her Nvidia equity, according to media reports, and Forbes said her net worth of $1.2 billion in mid-2026 put her in 32nd place on its list of America’s richest self-made women. Kress, who holds an undergraduate degree in finance and an MBA, was also named among the 50 most powerful women in business on rankings compiled by Fortune and Forbes magazines in recent years. Nvidia’s CEO turmoil comes as the company is set to report its third-quarter earnings next Tuesday.
