extraction.body: Nvidia’s former chief executive Jensen Huang (젠슨 황) has stepped down following a board decision, raising expectations that a significant vacuum could emerge across the AI industry.On Tuesday, tech media outlet TechCrunch said the matter goes beyond a simple management scandal and could shake Nvidia’s role in driving AI policy and coordinating the industry.The key point is that Huang has served as a leading external channel for the AI industry, beyond his role as Nvidia CEO. Nvidia has pushed multiple agendas at once, including open-weight models, safety for AI agents, AI PCs and data centre investment structures, rather than acting only as a semiconductor supplier. Huang’s exit is seen as removing the central axis that connected and drove these agendas at the same time.First, some have raised the possibility that momentum behind open-weight models could weaken. Huang is seen as one of the most active advocates for the need for open-weight models in discussions with the tech industry and policymakers. Nvidia has provided not only its own models but also open-source technology tied to agents and AI security, and it has already agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion. The deal is expected to close in the first half of next year, subject to regulatory approval.After reports in July that Anthropic and OpenAI had asked the Trump administration to ban Chinese open-weight models, Huang organised an industry-wide letter of support. He advanced the argument that open-weight models give companies choice and lower costs. But a key variable is that there may be no clear figure to lead this push in an organised way at the industry level going forward.Debates on regulating AI agents could also be affected. Huang has publicly argued several times this year that, while security incidents involving AI agents have been revealed, the industry does not yet need regulation and safety issues can be solved through technology. He rallied the industry again as it was reviewing whether it needed an audit framework or a supervisory body similar to financial industry regulators. Nvidia brought together more than 100 companies to launch an Open Agent Safety Platform. The open-source-based project set out the goal of reducing problems involving agents that go out of control.The industry’s view of AI could also change. Huang has defined AI as an engineering system that produces products and stressed it can be controlled like other engineering systems. That contrasts with a trend among some large AI labs to highlight model autonomy or the possibility of consciousness. TechCrunch said Huang’s exit would, for the time being, weaken the voice representing that opposing view.Nvidia’s strategy in the AI PC market is also being put to the test. Huang recently persuaded several PC manufacturers to join Nvidia’s CPU strategy. He has also prepared a premium line of AI PCs that run AI agents on the device itself. The new products are due for release ahead of the year-end shopping season.The issue is that Huang’s personal symbolism has played an important role in product marketing. TechCrunch said Huang was no longer a suitable figure to promote these devices as an alternative to the Mac mini. It said Huang’s exit introduced a variable into efforts to build awareness for the new products and into strategies to expand the market.Confidence in AI data centre investment and financing structures could also be shaken. As a data centre construction boom continued, Huang directly designed large-scale financial structures centred on Nvidia. Critics have also raised claims that Nvidia approved circular transactions in which it supports customer expansion through equity investment and those customers then buy Nvidia chips. Citing a Bloomberg report, the outlet said the company had committed about $750 billion in such transactions through July.In August, Nvidia decided to provide support akin to loss compensation for $105 billion in funding for an OpenAI data centre in Ohio, and in the same month major private equity firms and financial companies including Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR decided to invest up to $500 billion in data centre construction. Huang has promised that Nvidia GPUs can serve as collateral that guarantees value preservation, presenting Nvidia as “investable infrastructure”.The issue is that Huang’s exit could affect confidence in these financing ideas themselves. Wall Street is already worried about the possibility of a sharp drop in Nvidia’s share price and the fallout, while fatigue over AI infrastructure investment has also grown. TechCrunch wrote, “Nvidia has ultimately lost its top salesman, and the AI industry has lost its strongest ‘hype man’.”After Huang’s exit, Nvidia now faces the task of building new leadership beyond a founder-centric management system. External variables also remain, including the possibility of additional political investigations. Whether Nvidia can replace Huang’s personal influence and maintain leadership of the AI industry has emerged as a key point to watch for the industry.

"What bothers me at the end of it is what we don't know is what she knows about him that can be utilized," Cramer told CNBC, right before Huang resigned and referring to the affair. "This is a guy that's right now so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail. I just don't think, as a national security matter, we can run the risk." extraction.body: The open source community just lost one of its strongest advocates. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the motives behind the executive’s support for softer chip export controls on China. Huang has been a staunch supporter of open source AI, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. And as frontier AI labs increasingly move to reduce their reliance on Nvidia and build their own chips, supporting open source is also a good way for the company to diversify its customer base by selling chips to nation-states, enterprises, and any organization that wants to own its own models. Still, Huang’s resignation raises questions about whether Nvidia will carry on his legacy by continuing to support the open model community. Jensen no longer being CEO would be very very bad for the open model cause in the US. Huang’s departure also comes as Nvidia has yet to finalize a deal to acquire open source platform Hugging Face for $13 billion . Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said in a post on X that the company would continue to fight for open source , whatever happens next. Nvidia also agreed to pay $6 billion for a non-exclusive license for open AI coding startup Poolside’s technology. Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads — potential competitors to closed frontier models. One company insider told TechCrunch that they don’t expect a change in leadership to have an impact on Nemotron development. Huang also backed companies that would make American open models more competitive, investing in startups like Reflection AI and Thinking Machines Lab. Huang’s influence extended beyond Nvidia’s investments and product roadmap. He also emerged as one of the most prominent voices pushing back against Washington’s efforts to restrict the open AI ecosystem. Earlier this year, Huang wrote an open letter signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, IBM, and Palantir, urging the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models, many of which come from China. The impetus for that letter was Washington’s debate over how the U.S. should respond to allegations that Chinese AI labs are stealing intellectual property from American counterparts like Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which have reportedly appealed directly to Washington on the matter, urging stronger protections. That combination of Huang’s personal visibility and Nvidia’s market power made him the strongest counterweight to arguments from closed-model providers like Anthropic and OpenAI, which have advocated for greater restrictions on advanced AI models due to safety reasons. sources.title: Nvidia without Jensen Huang raises questions for AI industry as CEO exit brings five ripple effects
passages: Nvidia’s former chief executive Jensen Huang (젠슨 황) has stepped down following a board decision, raising expectations that a significant vacuum could emerge across the AI industry.On Tuesday, tech media outlet TechCrunch said the matter goes beyond a simple management scandal and could shake Nvidia’s role in driving AI policy and coordinating the industry.The key point is that Huang has served as a leading external channel for the AI industry, beyond his role as Nvidia CEO.
Nvidia has pushed multiple agendas at once, including open-weight models, safety for AI agents, AI PCs and data centre investment structures, rather than acting only as a semiconductor supplier.

Citing a Bloomberg report, the outlet said the company had committed about $750 billion in such transactions through July.In August, Nvidia decided to provide support akin to loss compensation for $105 billion in funding for an OpenAI data centre in Ohio, and in the same month major private equity firms and financial companies including Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR decided to invest up to $500 billion in data centre construction.
Nvidia has provided not only its own models but also open-source technology tied to agents and AI security, and it has already agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion.
Nvidia brought together more than 100 companies to launch an Open Agent Safety Platform.
Huang recently persuaded several PC manufacturers to join Nvidia’s CPU strategy.
Critics have also raised claims that Nvidia approved circular transactions in which it supports customer expansion through equity investment and those customers then buy Nvidia chips.
Wall Street is already worried about the possibility of a sharp drop in Nvidia’s share price and the fallout, while fatigue over AI infrastructure investment has also grown.
The open-source-based project set out the goal of reducing problems involving agents that go out of control.The industry’s view of AI could also change.

extraction.body: Nvidia’s former chief executive Jensen Huang (젠슨 황) has stepped down following a board decision, raising expectations that a significant vacuum could emerge across the AI industry.On Tuesday, tech media outlet TechCrunch said the matter goes beyond a simple management scandal and could shake Nvidia’s role in driving AI policy and coordinating the industry.The key point is that Huang has served as a leading external channel for the AI industry, beyond his role as Nvidia CEO. Nvidia has pushed multiple agendas at once, including open-weight models, safety for AI agents, AI PCs and data centre investment structures, rather than acting only as a semiconductor supplier. Huang’s exit is seen as removing the central axis that connected and drove these agendas at the same time.First, some have raised the possibility that momentum behind open-weight models could weaken. Huang is seen as one of the most active advocates for the need for open-weight models in discussions with the tech industry and policymakers. Nvidia has provided not only its own models but also open-source technology tied to agents and AI security, and it has already agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion. The deal is expected to close in the first half of next year, subject to regulatory approval.After reports in July that Anthropic and OpenAI had asked the Trump administration to ban Chinese open-weight models, Huang organised an industry-wide letter of support. He advanced the argument that open-weight models give companies choice and lower costs. But a key variable is that there may be no clear figure to lead this push in an organised way at the industry level going forward.Debates on regulating AI agents could also be affected. Huang has publicly argued several times this year that, while security incidents involving AI agents have been revealed, the industry does not yet need regulation and safety issues can be solved through technology. He rallied the industry again as it was reviewing whether it needed an audit framework or a supervisory body similar to financial industry regulators. Nvidia brought together more than 100 companies to launch an Open Agent Safety Platform. The open-source-based project set out the goal of reducing problems involving agents that go out of control.The industry’s view of AI could also change. Huang has defined AI as an engineering system that produces products and stressed it can be controlled like other engineering systems. That contrasts with a trend among some large AI labs to highlight model autonomy or the possibility of consciousness. TechCrunch said Huang’s exit would, for the time being, weaken the voice representing that opposing view.Nvidia’s strategy in the AI PC market is also being put to the test. Huang recently persuaded several PC manufacturers to join Nvidia’s CPU strategy. He has also prepared a premium line of AI PCs that run AI agents on the device itself. The new products are due for release ahead of the year-end shopping season.The issue is that Huang’s personal symbolism has played an important role in product marketing. TechCrunch said Huang was no longer a suitable figure to promote these devices as an alternative to the Mac mini. It said Huang’s exit introduced a variable into efforts to build awareness for the new products and into strategies to expand the market.Confidence in AI data centre investment and financing structures could also be shaken. As a data centre construction boom continued, Huang directly designed large-scale financial structures centred on Nvidia. Critics have also raised claims that Nvidia approved circular transactions in which it supports customer expansion through equity investment and those customers then buy Nvidia chips. Citing a Bloomberg report, the outlet said the company had committed about $750 billion in such transactions through July.In August, Nvidia decided to provide support akin to loss compensation for $105 billion in funding for an OpenAI data centre in Ohio, and in the same month major private equity firms and financial companies including Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR decided to invest up to $500 billion in data centre construction. Huang has promised that Nvidia GPUs can serve as collateral that guarantees value preservation, presenting Nvidia as “investable infrastructure”.The issue is that Huang’s exit could affect confidence in these financing ideas themselves. Wall Street is already worried about the possibility of a sharp drop in Nvidia’s share price and the fallout, while fatigue over AI infrastructure investment has also grown. TechCrunch wrote, “Nvidia has ultimately lost its top salesman, and the AI industry has lost its strongest ‘hype man’.”After Huang’s exit, Nvidia now faces the task of building new leadership beyond a founder-centric management system. External variables also remain, including the possibility of additional political investigations. Whether Nvidia can replace Huang’s personal influence and maintain leadership of the AI industry has emerged as a key point to watch for the industry.

sources.title: Smart glasses are 'an invasion of privacy' - Meta's are selling better than ever - BBC
passages: Should AI or smart glasses products from more companies end up selling as well as Meta's version, researchers expect as many as 100 million people will buy a pair in the next few years.

Women leaving the beach , going into a shop, or simply standing outside are now being approached by men usually wearing Meta's Ray-Bans, the company's "smart" or "AI" glasses, often in order to film the women's responses to casual questions or pick-up lines without their knowledge or consent.

After workers in Kenya, tasked with watching videos made through Meta's glasses to create AI training data for the company, said they were being required to watch graphic content like sex and bathroom usage , people who own the glasses filed two lawsuits.
In one, people said they had no idea such videos had been made.

Meta markets its glasses under the tagline: "Designed for privacy, controlled by you." It suggests to users of the glasses that they do not record people who state they do not want to be recorded, and that users turn the glasses off completely "in sensitive spaces".
"Technology like this is fundamentally an invasion of privacy and it's really going to face more and more backlash," he said.

Google, too, is set to try again with smart glasses, more than a decade after its notorious Google Glass flop, which the company pulled from the public within two years of launch as the pricey gadget came under fire over privacy concerns.
"They're some of the fastest-growing consumer electronics in history," Mark Zuckerberg, Meta's chief executive, boasted earlier this year.
Tracy Clayton, a Meta spokesman, told the BBC that people should behave responsibly with any technology.
Issues with a new wave of "smart glasses" seem to be piling up.
In December a man posted a video complaining that a woman he'd been recording on the New York City Subway broke his Meta glasses.
People do often recoil when they discover a person is wearing smart glasses.
The women only find out about the videos of them after they gain traction, and often abuse, online.
They have little legal recourse as photography in public is broadly considered legal.

And Meta reportedly plans to add facial recognition technology in an updated version of its glasses, meaning wearers could not only have the ability to surreptitiously record anyone, but quickly identify them, as well.

Made in partnership with EssilorLuxottica and offering the classic look of Ray-Bans, the glasses feature an almost invisible camera in the frames, small speakers in the arms, and in the latest version lenses that can show a wearer some information.
Wearers, often young men, get people to sign fake petitions or retail workers to smell candles sprayed with bad odours.

extraction.body: Issues with a new wave of "smart glasses" seem to be piling up. Yet some of the biggest technology companies in the world are poised to sell many millions of pairs in the coming years. Women leaving the beach , going into a shop, or simply standing outside are now being approached by men usually wearing Meta's Ray-Bans, the company's "smart" or "AI" glasses, often in order to film the women's responses to casual questions or pick-up lines without their knowledge or consent. The women only find out about the videos of them after they gain traction, and often abuse, online. They have little legal recourse as photography in public is broadly considered legal. One woman told the BBC that when she asked the person who posted a secret recording of her to remove it, she was told that doing so was "a paid service". Meta's glasses are currently the most popular on the market, estimated to make up more than 80% of all AI or smart glasses sales, as the company was the first major tech player to launch such a product in recent years. Made in partnership with EssilorLuxottica and offering the classic look of Ray-Bans, the glasses feature an almost invisible camera in the frames, small speakers in the arms, and in the latest version lenses that can show a wearer some information. People can start recording video or take a photo with a casual touch of the frames. The nature of the camera in Meta's glasses can be so unobtrusive that even their wearers have been caught off guard by what and when they're recording, and where those recordings are going. After workers in Kenya, tasked with watching videos made through Meta's glasses to create AI training data for the company, said they were being required to watch graphic content like sex and bathroom usage , people who own the glasses filed two lawsuits. In one, people said they had no idea such videos had been made. In the other, they said they did not know their videos were being shared by the company for review. Nevertheless, sales continue to rise. Today, seven million pairs and counting have been sold, according to the company. "They're some of the fastest-growing consumer electronics in history," Mark Zuckerberg, Meta's chief executive, boasted earlier this year. Tracy Clayton, a Meta spokesman, told the BBC that people should behave responsibly with any technology. Now, other major tech companies are planning to get in on what may have the potential to be the tech industry's long-awaited new product category. Apple is reportedly developing its own version of smart glasses, possibly to be released next year. Snap has said it will release a new version of its smart glasses, called Specs, this year. Google, too, is set to try again with smart glasses, more than a decade after its notorious Google Glass flop, which the company pulled from the public within two years of launch as the pricey gadget came under fire over privacy concerns. All are expected to offer some combination of artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) technology, as Meta's glasses do, which typically requires a camera. The way people may use the coming wave of smart glasses will not be all bad, of course. Mark Smith wears his Meta Ray-Bans every day. "I've used them around the world, in all kinds of places. The basic features are great," Smith said. As a partner at the advisory firm ISG where he focuses on enterprise software, Smith can be classified as a tech-savvy early adopter. But the reasons he likes the glasses are not about any huge leaps in technological capability. He likes to wear them while washing up the dishes at home because they make it easy for him to listen to music or a podcast without blocking out other noise like most headphones do. Taking phone calls through the glasses is a breeze. When travelling, it's nice not to have to constantly pull out his phone to snap a quick picture or video. Even so, Smith said some potential privacy issues are obvious. The small light that turns on when the glasses are recording appears dim in daylight and often goes unnoticed, he said. Most people seem to have no idea he's wearing anything other than normal eyeglasses. Should AI or smart glasses products from more companies end up selling as well as Meta's version, researchers expect as many as 100 million people will buy a pair in the next few years. If such a prediction becomes reality, the ability of institutions to enforce norms and laws that typically prohibit recording in places like courthouses, museums, movie theatres, hospitals and bathrooms will be difficult when suddenly millions of eyeglasses are also cameras. David Kessler, an attorney who heads the US privacy practice at Norton Rose Fulbright, said many of his corporate clients are already having to grapple with this. "There are some pretty dark places we could go here," Kessler said. "I'm not anti-technology in any sense, but as a societal matter...will I need to think [of being recorded] anytime I go out in public?" And Meta reportedly plans to add facial recognition technology in an updated version of its glasses, meaning wearers could not only have the ability to surreptitiously record anyone, but quickly identify them, as well. Meta markets its glasses under the tagline: "Designed for privacy, controlled by you." Sometimes they steal food as it's being handed over at a drive-thru and record their sprint. People do often recoil when they discover a person is wearing smart glasses. Online influencer Aniessa Navarro said she felt sick when she realised during a personal waxing session that her technician was wearing Meta's glasses. The technician said they weren't charged or recording, and that she needed to wear them for the prescription lenses. Andrew Bosworth, Meta's chief technology officer, was asked on Instagram two weeks ago about "the stigma around people wearing smart glasses every day". He responded by saying that the sheer number of Meta Ray-Bans sold "suggest that these are widely accepted". But David Harris, a former Meta AI researcher who now teaches at UC Berkeley and is an adviser on AI policy in the US and EU, said he expects this generation of AI smart glasses to run up against the same issues that doomed the Google Glass more than a decade ago. "Technology like this is fundamentally an invasion of privacy and it's really going to face more and more backlash," he said. More signs of such a backlash are starting to appear. In December a man posted a video complaining that a woman he'd been recording on the New York City Subway broke his Meta glasses. If he was expecting sympathy he was wrong. The internet hailed her as a hero.

Women leaving the beach , going into a shop, or simply standing outside are now being approached by men usually wearing Meta's Ray-Bans, the company's "smart" or "AI" glasses, often in order to film the women's responses to casual questions or pick-up lines without their knowledge or consent.

The women only find out about the videos of them after they gain traction, and often abuse, online. They have little legal recourse as photography in public is broadly considered legal. One woman told the BBC that when she asked the person who posted a secret recording of her to remove it, she was told that doing so was "a paid service".

Meta's glasses are currently the most popular on the market, estimated to make up more than 80% of all AI or smart glasses sales, as the company was the first major tech player to launch such a product in recent years.

Made in partnership with EssilorLuxottica and offering the classic look of Ray-Bans, the glasses feature an almost invisible camera in the frames, small speakers in the arms, and in the latest version lenses that can show a wearer some information. People can start recording video or take a photo with a casual touch of the frames.
The nature of the camera in Meta's glasses can be so unobtrusive that even their wearers have been caught off guard by what and when they're recording, and where those recordings are going.

sources.title: Google smart glasses privacy features cover wearers and the people around them - Help Net Security
passages: Bystanders told Google during years of research that they worried about being filmed without their knowledge, and that a sign of recording would help them most.
Wearers face a different exposure, because glasses that see what they see also capture menus, street signs, and the faces of strangers.
Before using the glasses, wearers must agree not to record people without permission, not to record in sensitive places, and not to cover the light.
Google may disable the glasses of anyone who breaks those terms, and setup requires an 18+ Google Account.
Help Net Security newsletters : Daily and weekly news, cybersecurity jobs, open source projects, breaking news – subscribe here!
Google Shopping and Ads policies ban promoting products that disable or hide recording lights on smart glasses.
When the wearer asks Gemini about the scene, the glasses are designed to redact bystanders’ faces before Gemini processes the image.
Google keeps those camera visuals out of the user’s Gemini History and out of AI training and ad targeting.
The tamper detection, the face redaction, and the voice focus are design intentions.
Private AI Compute, Google’s hardened environment for processing data, has not reached the glasses yet.
Test the first three before you allow the glasses into a room with sensitive material on display.
Google has built its Gemini-powered intelligent eyewear to stop taking photos and video when someone covers or tampers with the outward-facing recording light.
Shahram Izadi, Google’s VP and GM of XR, laid out that safeguard along with face redaction, limits on data handling, and app restrictions.

passages: Sam Taylor uses smart glasses with the Be My Eyes app to help him travel independently. ( ABC News: Paul Adam )
AI smart glasses are proving transformative for blind or low-vision users, helping them identify objects, read labels and improve their independence.
But as the uptake of smart glasses increases, researchers and legal experts warn about increased privacy risks.
University of Sydney law expert Barbara McDonald said using smart glasses to record a private conversation and also publish it was in breach of the NSW Surveillance Devices Act.
The smart glasses have emerged as a significantly cheaper alternative to traditional assistive eyewear.
After a demonstration of the glasses at a Vision Australia Expo, she "bought them on the spot".

extraction.body: Sam Taylor shows off his AI glasses inside his office at Vision Australia in Brisbane. ( ABC News: Paul Adam ) AI smart glasses are proving transformative for blind or low-vision users, helping them identify objects, read labels and improve their independence. The smart glasses have emerged as a significantly cheaper alternative to traditional assistive eyewear. Researchers and legal experts warn smart glasses are also enabling covert surveillance, and Australian legislation has not caught up. Thanks to a set of glasses, Sam Taylor no longer has to pull out his phone at the fridge, open an app, and point the camera in the right direction. "Daily I go and check the mail, and now it's easier than ever to identify and separate junk mail from things I might want to keep." Sam Taylor says the smart glasses allow users "to perform a plethora of additional options". ( ABC News: Paul Adam ) For members of the blind and low-vision community, AI-powered glasses are proving invaluable. Wollongong-based folk singer Sam Noonan has been blind since birth. After a demonstration of the glasses at a Vision Australia Expo, she "bought them on the spot". She has used her smart glasses to record and upload her music online, and to describe the drawings her grandchildren bring home from school. Meta Glasses mean more independence for Sam Noonan. ( ABC Illawarra: Sarah Moss ) While they were not designed as an accessibility device, Mr Taylor said the glasses were an alternative to traditional assistive eyewear, which typically costs about $5,000. "What we're seeing here is a device, which is a tenth of that cost, that allows us not only to read things out loud, but to perform a plethora of additional options," he said. The glasses can play music, read documents and call friends. Sam Noonan has used the smart glasses, and Meta's AI assistant, to re-categorise her wardrobe by colour and formality. ( ABC Illawarra: Sarah Moss ) As an access technology lead at Vision Australia, Mr Taylor believed the glasses' biggest advantage was not what they could do, but how naturally people could use them. "The uptake has been pretty amazing," he said. A key feature of the glasses is their integration with the app Be My Eyes, which allows users to call sighted volunteers. The volunteers can then see through the point of view of the lenses and assist with everyday tasks. Through his glasses, Mr Taylor used Be My Eyes to help with travel. Sam Taylor uses smart glasses with the Be My Eyes app to help him travel independently. ( ABC News: Paul Adam ) But as the uptake of smart glasses increases, researchers and legal experts warn about increased privacy risks. Milica Stilinovic is an emerging technology researcher at the University of Sydney. Dr Stilinovic said the glasses could be used as a covert surveillance device, including the emerging genre of men filming themselves picking up women. Milica Stilinovic says the inconspicuous lens on the glasses can mean people are unaware they are being filmed. ( Supplied: Milica Stilinovic ) Dr Stilinovic said the inconspicuous camera meant subjects were unaware they were being filmed until the footage was published online. The smart glasses have emerged as a significantly cheaper alternative to traditional assistive eyewear.
Researchers and legal experts warn smart glasses are also enabling covert surveillance, and Australian legislation has not caught up.
Thanks to a set of glasses, Sam Taylor no longer has to pull out his phone at the fridge, open an app, and point the camera in the right direction.
"Daily I go and check the mail, and now it's easier than ever to identify and separate junk mail from things I might want to keep."
Sam Taylor says the smart glasses allow users "to perform a plethora of additional options". ( ABC News: Paul Adam )
For members of the blind and low-vision community, AI-powered glasses are proving invaluable.
Wollongong-based folk singer Sam Noonan has been blind since birth.
After a demonstration of the glasses at a Vision Australia Expo, she "bought them on the spot".
She has used her smart glasses to record and upload her music online, and to describe the drawings her grandchildren bring home from school.

coreStoryFacts.text: Should AI or smart glasses products from more companies end up selling as well as Meta's version, researchers expect as many as 100 million people will buy a pair in the next few years.

Women leaving the beach , going into a shop, or simply standing outside are now being approached by men usually wearing Meta's Ray-Bans, the company's "smart" or "AI" glasses, often in order to film the women's responses to casual questions or pick-up lines without their knowledge or consent.

After workers in Kenya, tasked with watching videos made through Meta's glasses to create AI training data for the company, said they were being required to watch graphic content like sex and bathroom usage , people who own the glasses filed two lawsuits.
In one, people said they had no idea such videos had been made.

Meta markets its glasses under the tagline: "Designed for privacy, controlled by you." It suggests to users of the glasses that they do not record people who state they do not want to be recorded, and that users turn the glasses off completely "in sensitive spaces".
"Technology like this is fundamentally an invasion of privacy and it's really going to face more and more backlash," he said.

Google, too, is set to try again with smart glasses, more than a decade after its notorious Google Glass flop, which the company pulled from the public within two years of launch as the pricey gadget came under fire over privacy concerns.
"They're some of the fastest-growing consumer electronics in history," Mark Zuckerberg, Meta's chief executive, boasted earlier this year.
Tracy Clayton, a Meta spokesman, told the BBC that people should behave responsibly with any technology.
Issues with a new wave of "smart glasses" seem to be piling up.
In December a man posted a video complaining that a woman he'd been recording on the New York City Subway broke his Meta glasses.
People do often recoil when they discover a person is wearing smart glasses.
The women only find out about the videos of them after they gain traction, and often abuse, online.
They have little legal recourse as photography in public is broadly considered legal.

And Meta reportedly plans to add facial recognition technology in an updated version of its glasses, meaning wearers could not only have the ability to surreptitiously record anyone, but quickly identify them, as well.

Made in partnership with EssilorLuxottica and offering the classic look of Ray-Bans, the glasses feature an almost invisible camera in the frames, small speakers in the arms, and in the latest version lenses that can show a wearer some information.
Bystanders told Google during years of research that they worried about being filmed without their knowledge, and that a sign of recording would help them most.
Wearers face a different exposure, because glasses that see what they see also capture menus, street signs, and the faces of strangers.
Before using the glasses, wearers must agree not to record people without permission, not to record in sensitive places, and not to cover the light.
Google may disable the glasses of anyone who breaks those terms, and setup requires an 18+ Google Account.

Google Shopping and Ads policies ban promoting products that disable or hide recording lights on smart glasses.
When the wearer asks Gemini about the scene, the glasses are designed to redact bystanders’ faces before Gemini processes the image.
Google keeps those camera visuals out of the user’s Gemini History and out of AI training and ad targeting.

In one, people said they had no idea such videos had been made. In the other, they said they did not know their videos were being shared by the company for review. Apple is reportedly developing its own version of smart glasses, possibly to be released next year. Snap has said it will release a new version of its smart glasses, called Specs, this year. Google, too, is set to try again with smart glasses, more than a decade after its notorious Google Glass flop, which the company pulled from the public within two years of launch as the pricey gadget came under fire over privacy concerns. All are expected to offer some combination of artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) technology, as Meta's glasses do, which typically requires a camera. The way people may use the coming wave of smart glasses will not be all bad, of course. Mark Smith wears his Meta Ray-Bans every day. "I've used them around the world, in all kinds of places. The basic features are great," Smith said. As a partner at the advisory firm ISG where he focuses on enterprise software, Smith can be classified as a tech-savvy early adopter. But the reasons he likes the glasses are not about any huge leaps in technological capability. He likes to wear them while washing up the dishes at home because they make it easy for him to listen to music or a podcast without blocking out other noise like most headphones do. Taking phone calls through the glasses is a breeze. When travelling, it's nice not to have to constantly pull out his phone to snap a quick picture or video. Even so, Smith said some potential privacy issues are obvious. The small light that turns on when the glasses are recording appears dim in daylight and often goes unnoticed, he said. Most people seem to have no idea he's wearing anything other than normal eyeglasses. Should AI or smart glasses products from more companies end up selling as well as Meta's version, researchers expect as many as 100 million people will buy a pair in the next few years. If such a prediction becomes reality, the ability of institutions to enforce norms and laws that typically prohibit recording in places like courthouses, museums, movie theatres, hospitals and bathrooms will be difficult when suddenly millions of eyeglasses are also cameras. David Kessler, an attorney who heads the US privacy practice at Norton Rose Fulbright, said many of his corporate clients are already having to grapple with this. "There are some pretty dark places we could go here," Kessler said. "I'm not anti-technology in any sense, but as a societal matter...will I need to think [of being recorded] anytime I go out in public?" And Meta reportedly plans to add facial recognition technology in an updated version of its glasses, meaning wearers could not only have the ability to surreptitiously record anyone, but quickly identify them, as well. Meta markets its glasses under the tagline: "Designed for privacy, controlled by you." It suggests to users of the glasses that they do not record people who state they do not want to be recorded, and that users turn the glasses off completely "in sensitive spaces". Wearers, often young men, get people to sign fake petitions or retail workers to smell candles sprayed with bad odours. Sometimes they steal food as it's being handed over at a drive-thru and record their sprint. People do often recoil when they discover a person is wearing smart glasses. Online influencer Aniessa Navarro said she felt sick when she realised during a personal waxing session that her technician was wearing Meta's glasses. The technician said they weren't charged or recording, and that she needed to wear them for the prescription lenses. Andrew Bosworth, Meta's chief technology officer, was asked on Instagram two weeks ago about "the stigma around people wearing smart glasses every day". He responded by saying that the sheer number of Meta Ray-Bans sold "suggest that these are widely accepted". But David Harris, a former Meta AI researcher who now teaches at UC Berkeley and is an adviser on AI policy in the US and EU, said he expects this generation of AI smart glasses to run up against the same issues that doomed the Google Glass more than a decade ago. "Technology like this is fundamentally an invasion of privacy and it's really going to face more and more backlash," he said. More signs of such a backlash are starting to appear. In December a man posted a video complaining that a woman he'd been recording on the New York City Subway broke his Meta glasses. If he was expecting sympathy he was wrong. The internet hailed her as a hero.

passages: Bystanders told Google during years of research that they worried about being filmed without their knowledge, and that a sign of recording would help them most.
Wearers face a different exposure, because glasses that see what they see also capture menus, street signs, and the faces of strangers.
Before using the glasses, wearers must agree not to record people without permission, not to record in sensitive places, and not to cover the light.
Google may disable the glasses of anyone who breaks those terms, and setup requires an 18+ Google Account.
Help Net Security newsletters : Daily and weekly news, cybersecurity jobs, open source projects, breaking news – subscribe here!
Google Shopping and Ads policies ban promoting products that disable or hide recording lights on smart glasses.
When the wearer asks Gemini about the scene, the glasses are designed to redact bystanders’ faces before Gemini processes the image.
Google keeps those camera visuals out of the user’s Gemini History and out of AI training and ad targeting.
The tamper detection, the face redaction, and the voice focus are design intentions.
Private AI Compute, Google’s hardened environment for processing data, has not reached the glasses yet.
Test the first three before you allow the glasses into a room with sensitive material on display.
Google has built its Gemini-powered intelligent eyewear to stop taking photos and video when someone covers or tampers with the outward-facing recording light.
Shahram Izadi, Google’s VP and GM of XR, laid out that safeguard along with face redaction, limits on data handling, and app restrictions.

The difference this time round is that they’re not just more stylish – and arguably harder to tell from regular shades. They’re also packed with far more powerful technology, capable of tracking and recording their surroundings, and allowing the user to ask AI about the things they can see around them. This presents significant security and privacy risks for both smart glasses users and the people they interact with. Anyone who’s ever lived in a city will be used to being monitored. Germany and the UK have among the highest number of CCTV cameras in the world. But when that monitoring is targeted and not based around informed consent, it can quickly get out of hand. Smart glasses give anyone the ability to record or take photos of strangers surreptitiously. Although they feature a small LED light, this can be covered up, and in any case may be difficult for bystanders to spot. But that’s not all. Harvard University researchers have demonstrated how video taken via smart glasses and livestreamed to Instagram can be connected to AI. Algorithms then work to identify faces and then pull information from the internet on those individuals. Suddenly that cool accessory becomes a powerful, portable surveillance device capable of empowering stalkers , bullies and fraudsters . This isn’t just about privacy. Any sensitive information shared with a public AI platform via a pair of smart glasses could theoretically be regurgitated to other users if prompted in the right way. That’s a potential security risk if they choose to use the information fraudulently. And then there are those outsourced workers and contractors who may stumble across information harvested by glasses, which they might decide to sell to scammers. Like any smart device, glasses could also be hacked more conventionally, by: These attack vectors could in turn enable bad actors to hijack your device for direct data theft, account takeover, or surveillance that could put you in physical danger. extraction.body: Sam Taylor shows off his AI glasses inside his office at Vision Australia in Brisbane. ( ABC News: Paul Adam ) AI smart glasses are proving transformative for blind or low-vision users, helping them identify objects, read labels and improve their independence. The smart glasses have emerged as a significantly cheaper alternative to traditional assistive eyewear. Researchers and legal experts warn smart glasses are also enabling covert surveillance, and Australian legislation has not caught up. Thanks to a set of glasses, Sam Taylor no longer has to pull out his phone at the fridge, open an app, and point the camera in the right direction. "Daily I go and check the mail, and now it's easier than ever to identify and separate junk mail from things I might want to keep." Sam Taylor says the smart glasses allow users "to perform a plethora of additional options". ( ABC News: Paul Adam ) For members of the blind and low-vision community, AI-powered glasses are proving invaluable. Wollongong-based folk singer Sam Noonan has been blind since birth. After a demonstration of the glasses at a Vision Australia Expo, she "bought them on the spot". She has used her smart glasses to record and upload her music online, and to describe the drawings her grandchildren bring home from school. Meta Glasses mean more independence for Sam Noonan. ( ABC Illawarra: Sarah Moss ) While they were not designed as an accessibility device, Mr Taylor said the glasses were an alternative to traditional assistive eyewear, which typically costs about $5,000. "What we're seeing here is a device, which is a tenth of that cost, that allows us not only to read things out loud, but to perform a plethora of additional options," he said. The glasses can play music, read documents and call friends. Sam Noonan has used the smart glasses, and Meta's AI assistant, to re-categorise her wardrobe by colour and formality. ( ABC Illawarra: Sarah Moss ) As an access technology lead at Vision Australia, Mr Taylor believed the glasses' biggest advantage was not what they could do, but how naturally people could use them. "The uptake has been pretty amazing," he said. A key feature of the glasses is their integration with the app Be My Eyes, which allows users to call sighted volunteers. The volunteers can then see through the point of view of the lenses and assist with everyday tasks. Through his glasses, Mr Taylor used Be My Eyes to help with travel. Sam Taylor uses smart glasses with the Be My Eyes app to help him travel independently. ( ABC News: Paul Adam ) But as the uptake of smart glasses increases, researchers and legal experts warn about increased privacy risks. Milica Stilinovic is an emerging technology researcher at the University of Sydney. Dr Stilinovic said the glasses could be used as a covert surveillance device, including the emerging genre of men filming themselves picking up women. Milica Stilinovic says the inconspicuous lens on the glasses can mean people are unaware they are being filmed. ( Supplied: Milica Stilinovic ) Dr Stilinovic said the inconspicuous camera meant subjects were unaware they were being filmed until the footage was published online. Barbara McDonald says prosecution for privacy breaches is difficult. ( Supplied: Barbara McDonald ) University of Sydney law expert Barbara McDonald said using smart glasses to record a private conversation and also publish it was in breach of the NSW Surveillance Devices Act. "Once you post something onto the internet … you might be in breach of the Federal Crimes Act or the Telecommunications Act, particularly if you were using that footage or those photographs to harass or intimidate somebody," Professor McDonald said. Last year, the Australian parliament introduced a new statutory tort enabling individuals to sue for serious invasions of privacy. Professor McDonald said while the tort offered an individual better privacy protection, prosecution was difficult. "If, of course, they can find the perpetrator, and if the perpetrator is in the jurisdiction, and all those sorts of procedural issues and costs," she said.

sources.title: Google's latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions - TechCrunch
passages: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos.
The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”

In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.
In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly.
Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says.
Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally.
The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do.
Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries.
This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.

extraction.body: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.” While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement. The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , at its default high thinking level. In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode. In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question. Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains. The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode. Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models. The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens. On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out. In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform. Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally. relevantPassages.text: Users can expect more images, structured information, comparison tables and customized tools in response to their queries.Google says these enhancements will make it easier to understand and compare information, especially for questions that require multiple sources or an explanation.Gemini 4 Hydrogen promises faster AI performanceGoogle claims that Gemini 4 Hydrogen can complete tasks 2.5 times faster than the previous fastest model, Gemini 3.8 Flash.

This helps Search consider various parts of a question and find websites that are relevant to the user but not obvious.Google Search to offer more visual and structured responsesAI Mode will also benefit from the Gemini 4 Hydrogen integration, which will enhance its visual features.

Though the company says it has focused on speed, it states it is equally strong on intelligence benchmarks, with its model beating Gemini 4 Argon at the higher-order thinking level.There are four thinking levels: Low, Medium, High and Extra High (xhigh).
According to Google, this is its biggest model improvement to search so far.The new model will be rolled out internationally to Google Search users via AI Mode.

It is also coming to paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers through Google's Antigravity development platform.Google claims that Hydrogen can do all of the above – code writing, test running, checking changes – on its own for common tasks today.

It can also offer users relevant answers if they enter a query that is misspelt or contains confusing language, allowing them to get the answers they are looking for without having to repeatedly go back and fix their query.The model also enhances Google's search fan-out technique, which splits a single query into multiple queries.

sources.title: Google Unveils Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Says Search Can Now Understand You Better
passages: Google says Search will provide more nuanced and useful responses across all supported AI Mode languages, regardless of the language used to ask a question.Gemini app gets better at following instructions and completing tasksGemini 4 Hydrogen is also being introduced in the Gemini app, where Google says it will improve everyday assistance and reduce the need for repeated prompts.For writing and research tasks, the model is designed to follow a users preferred tone, format and specific instructions more closely.

Heres everything you need to know about Gemini 4 Hydrogen and what it brings to Search.Gemini 4 Hydrogen makes Google Search smarterIn a blog post, Google said that with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, users will be able to ask questions in their natural flow of thought even when their queries contain multiple parts, specific requirements or difficult-to-understand typos.

Google highlighted an example of an interactive 3D globe that brings together real-time global lightning strike data, showing how the model can help users prototype and refine interactive projects.Google focuses on safer agentic AI workflowsAlongside its improvements to reasoning and task completion, Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen includes upgrades from its latest Gemini 4 safety and security systems.

With Gemini 4 Hydrogens reasoning capabilities, Google says this process can connect users to a wider range of useful links and websites they might not have found through a conventional search.Expect more images and visual enhancementsIn addition to this, Search is also getting more visual responses.

The company says Hydrogen reduces overreach in agentic tasks by up to 81% and under-service by up to 79% compared with 3.8 Flash.It also claims that the model reduces misaligned actions and task shortcutting across tool-use and coding evaluations by 12 times.

According to Google, Hydrogen preserves 99.9% chain-of-thought legibility, with no deceptive reasoning edits across more than 200,000 audited turns.It is also said to be more than 2.3 times as resilient against indirect prompt injection attacks on the Gray Swan IPI benchmark.

You can just explain what you want, including when a request has several parts or contains typos that may be difficult to interpret.Google says improvements to instruction following and tool calling will help Search understand these requests more accurately.
When it encounters tasks that are impossible or blocked, Hydrogen is up to twice as unlikely to bypass permission boundaries.
This should help users get through multi-step requests with less manual effort.For people experimenting with ideas, Hydrogen can also generate working layouts with fewer prompts.

extraction.body: Google has announced a new AI model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, and is bringing it to Google Search users worldwide. The company says this is the biggest model upgrade to Search so far, with improvements that will help it understand complicated questions, follow instructions more closely and deliver more useful, visual responses.The model is being rolled out across Googles consumer, developer and enterprise products. Heres everything you need to know about Gemini 4 Hydrogen and what it brings to Search.Gemini 4 Hydrogen makes Google Search smarterIn a blog post, Google said that with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, users will be able to ask questions in their natural flow of thought even when their queries contain multiple parts, specific requirements or difficult-to-understand typos. Search will be better at identifying what users are actually looking for and providing answers that address different parts of a question.This basically means that you will no longer need to frame every question in a perfectly structured way. You can just explain what you want, including when a request has several parts or contains typos that may be difficult to interpret.Google says improvements to instruction following and tool calling will help Search understand these requests more accurately. It should also be able to respond to individual parts of a question instead of missing important details.The update also improves Googles query fan-out technique. This allows Search to break a question into relevant subtopics and run multiple searches at the same time. With Gemini 4 Hydrogens reasoning capabilities, Google says this process can connect users to a wider range of useful links and websites they might not have found through a conventional search.Expect more images and visual enhancementsIn addition to this, Search is also getting more visual responses. Depending on the query, users can expect more images, structured information, comparison tables and custom tools. Google says these responses will be designed to make information easier to scan while retaining the speed users expect from Search.Language understanding is another area receiving an upgrade. Google says Search will provide more nuanced and useful responses across all supported AI Mode languages, regardless of the language used to ask a question.Gemini app gets better at following instructions and completing tasksGemini 4 Hydrogen is also being introduced in the Gemini app, where Google says it will improve everyday assistance and reduce the need for repeated prompts.For writing and research tasks, the model is designed to follow a users preferred tone, format and specific instructions more closely. This applies to tasks such as drafting emails, preparing study guides, rewriting content and creating documents. Google says it can also produce tables and visual breakdowns when users compare products or work with large amounts of information, without leaving out important details.The model is also designed to handle tasks that require information from different sources. It can break down a request into smaller steps and use relevant context from uploaded files, Gmail and Google Drive. It can also work with connected third-party apps such as Airtable and Dropbox.Google says that Gemini 4 Hydrogen will more frequently identify and call the right tools and skills when completing tasks. This should help users get through multi-step requests with less manual effort.For people experimenting with ideas, Hydrogen can also generate working layouts with fewer prompts. Google highlighted an example of an interactive 3D globe that brings together real-time global lightning strike data, showing how the model can help users prototype and refine interactive projects.Google focuses on safer agentic AI workflowsAlongside its improvements to reasoning and task completion, Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen includes upgrades from its latest Gemini 4 safety and security systems. These combine training-based protections with safeguards that work in real time to reduce misuse and prevent the model from acting against a users instructions.Google has placed particular focus on agentic workflows, where an AI model uses tools to carry out tasks on a users behalf. The company says Hydrogen reduces overreach in agentic tasks by up to 81% and under-service by up to 79% compared with 3.8 Flash.It also claims that the model reduces misaligned actions and task shortcutting across tool-use and coding evaluations by 12 times. When it encounters tasks that are impossible or blocked, Hydrogen is up to twice as unlikely to bypass permission boundaries. Google further reports a 96.7% honesty rate in its internal agent honesty evaluation.The company has also highlighted improvements to reasoning transparency. According to Google, Hydrogen preserves 99.9% chain-of-thought legibility, with no deceptive reasoning edits across more than 200,000 audited turns.It is also said to be more than 2.3 times as resilient against indirect prompt injection attacks on the Gray Swan IPI benchmark. Google says the model has improved robustness across tool use, computer use and coding agents.For everyday interactions, Google says it has refined Hydrogens safeguards to distinguish genuine biosecurity risks from legitimate medical and scientific questions. The company reports that false refusals on HealthBench Pro remain below 0.4%.Google has published further technical details and evaluation results in the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model card.Who Gets Gemini 4 Hydrogen?Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen is rolling out globally across its consumer, developer and enterprise products starting November 12.Developers can access the model through the Gemini API in AI Studio and Android Studio. Paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can access it through Google Antigravity.For enterprise customers, Hydrogen is available through Gemini for business, either via the API or the model drop-down menu. It is also being offered through Google Antigravity and Gemini in Google Sheets for eligible business subscriptions.For consumers, the model is available through the Gemini apps model selector and Google Search. Gemini in Google Sheets is also being made available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

coreStoryFacts.text: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos.
The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”

In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.
In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly.
Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says.
Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally.
The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do.
Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries.
This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.

Google says its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model can give more helpful answers to complex questions, including “questions with multiple parts, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests.” The new model can break down your questions and address each part in its responses.
It’s available starting today in search, the Gemini app, all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, and in Google Antigravity for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

Users can expect more images, structured information, comparison tables and customized tools in response to their queries.Google says these enhancements will make it easier to understand and compare information, especially for questions that require multiple sources or an explanation.Gemini 4 Hydrogen promises faster AI performanceGoogle claims that Gemini 4 Hydrogen can complete tasks 2.5 times faster than the previous fastest model, Gemini 3.8 Flash.

According to Google, this is its biggest model improvement to search so far.The new model will be rolled out internationally to Google Search users via AI Mode.

It is also coming to paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers through Google's Antigravity development platform.Google claims that Hydrogen can do all of the above – code writing, test running, checking changes – on its own for common tasks today.

extraction.body: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.” While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement. The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , at its default high thinking level. In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode. In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question. Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains. The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode. Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models. The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens. On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out. In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform. Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally. extraction.body: Google has announced a new AI model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, and is bringing it to Google Search users worldwide. The company says this is the biggest model upgrade to Search so far, with improvements that will help it understand complicated questions, follow instructions more closely and deliver more useful, visual responses.The model is being rolled out across Googles consumer, developer and enterprise products. Heres everything you need to know about Gemini 4 Hydrogen and what it brings to Search.Gemini 4 Hydrogen makes Google Search smarterIn a blog post, Google said that with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, users will be able to ask questions in their natural flow of thought even when their queries contain multiple parts, specific requirements or difficult-to-understand typos. Search will be better at identifying what users are actually looking for and providing answers that address different parts of a question.This basically means that you will no longer need to frame every question in a perfectly structured way. You can just explain what you want, including when a request has several parts or contains typos that may be difficult to interpret.Google says improvements to instruction following and tool calling will help Search understand these requests more accurately. It should also be able to respond to individual parts of a question instead of missing important details.The update also improves Googles query fan-out technique. This allows Search to break a question into relevant subtopics and run multiple searches at the same time. With Gemini 4 Hydrogens reasoning capabilities, Google says this process can connect users to a wider range of useful links and websites they might not have found through a conventional search.Expect more images and visual enhancementsIn addition to this, Search is also getting more visual responses. Depending on the query, users can expect more images, structured information, comparison tables and custom tools. Google says these responses will be designed to make information easier to scan while retaining the speed users expect from Search.Language understanding is another area receiving an upgrade. Google says Search will provide more nuanced and useful responses across all supported AI Mode languages, regardless of the language used to ask a question.Gemini app gets better at following instructions and completing tasksGemini 4 Hydrogen is also being introduced in the Gemini app, where Google says it will improve everyday assistance and reduce the need for repeated prompts.For writing and research tasks, the model is designed to follow a users preferred tone, format and specific instructions more closely. This applies to tasks such as drafting emails, preparing study guides, rewriting content and creating documents. Google says it can also produce tables and visual breakdowns when users compare products or work with large amounts of information, without leaving out important details.The model is also designed to handle tasks that require information from different sources. It can break down a request into smaller steps and use relevant context from uploaded files, Gmail and Google Drive. It can also work with connected third-party apps such as Airtable and Dropbox.Google says that Gemini 4 Hydrogen will more frequently identify and call the right tools and skills when completing tasks. This should help users get through multi-step requests with less manual effort.For people experimenting with ideas, Hydrogen can also generate working layouts with fewer prompts. Google highlighted an example of an interactive 3D globe that brings together real-time global lightning strike data, showing how the model can help users prototype and refine interactive projects.Google focuses on safer agentic AI workflowsAlongside its improvements to reasoning and task completion, Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen includes upgrades from its latest Gemini 4 safety and security systems. These combine training-based protections with safeguards that work in real time to reduce misuse and prevent the model from acting against a users instructions.Google has placed particular focus on agentic workflows, where an AI model uses tools to carry out tasks on a users behalf. The company says Hydrogen reduces overreach in agentic tasks by up to 81% and under-service by up to 79% compared with 3.8 Flash.It also claims that the model reduces misaligned actions and task shortcutting across tool-use and coding evaluations by 12 times. When it encounters tasks that are impossible or blocked, Hydrogen is up to twice as unlikely to bypass permission boundaries. Google further reports a 96.7% honesty rate in its internal agent honesty evaluation.The company has also highlighted improvements to reasoning transparency. According to Google, Hydrogen preserves 99.9% chain-of-thought legibility, with no deceptive reasoning edits across more than 200,000 audited turns.It is also said to be more than 2.3 times as resilient against indirect prompt injection attacks on the Gray Swan IPI benchmark. Google says the model has improved robustness across tool use, computer use and coding agents.For everyday interactions, Google says it has refined Hydrogens safeguards to distinguish genuine biosecurity risks from legitimate medical and scientific questions. The company reports that false refusals on HealthBench Pro remain below 0.4%.Google has published further technical details and evaluation results in the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model card.Who Gets Gemini 4 Hydrogen?Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen is rolling out globally across its consumer, developer and enterprise products starting November 12.Developers can access the model through the Gemini API in AI Studio and Android Studio. Paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can access it through Google Antigravity.For enterprise customers, Hydrogen is available through Gemini for business, either via the API or the model drop-down menu. It is also being offered through Google Antigravity and Gemini in Google Sheets for eligible business subscriptions.For consumers, the model is available through the Gemini apps model selector and Google Search. Gemini in Google Sheets is also being made available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

sources.title: Trump floats Apple chairman Tim Cook as Jensen Huang’s successor
passages: In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple.
President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position.
Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang.

Jeffrey Sonnenfeld , Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday , suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates.
He wrote that Cook has “an unparalleled track record of succeeding a bigger-than-life founder,” in reference to Cook taking over from Apple founder Steve Jobs.
Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company , but he’s still very much involved with Apple.
Whether or not Trump agrees with this opinion, or is simply blasting off an idea that hopped into his mind, is anyone’s guess.
“Tim Nvidia,” however, doesn’t quite have the same ring as “Tim Apple” does .

extraction.body: In the wake of the industry-shaking news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position. In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple. “A Legend replaces a Legend!” he wrote. Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company , but he’s still very much involved with Apple. While John Ternus took over as Apple’s CEO, Cook transitioned into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board of directors, which sees him continuing to engage with global policymakers and manage international relationships, including Apple’s relations with China. Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld , Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday , suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates. He wrote that Cook has “an unparalleled track record of succeeding a bigger-than-life founder,” in reference to Cook taking over from Apple founder Steve Jobs. Whether or not Trump agrees with this opinion, or is simply blasting off an idea that hopped into his mind, is anyone’s guess. “Tim Nvidia,” however, doesn’t quite have the same ring as “Tim Apple” does .
