extraction.body: Singapore, a hub for billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia sales each year, finds itself increasingly in the crosshairs of Washington's push to stop advanced AI chips from reaching China, as the chipmaker CEO's scandal once again thrusts the city-state into the spotlight. The Southeast Asian nation said Thursday that it had barred Alice Huang, the businesswoman at the center of a scandal that catalyzed the end of Jensen Huang's run as Nvidia CEO, from re-entering the country. A fifth person was handed 41 charges on Friday in a Singapore fraud case involving computer servers that might have contained Nvidia chips and were exported to Malaysia. The alleged transactions in the broader case totaled about $390 million, prosecutors said March last year. The investigations into several companies and key officials, including Megaspeed International, began in February 2025 and remained ongoing as of Thursday. Authorities have been examining whether servers exported through Singapore to Malaysia without entering the domestic market were subsequently rerouted to another destination, contrary to declarations made in Singapore, the Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement late Thursday. Singapore has faced growing international scrutiny, particularly from the U.S., over its role as a major billing and potential transit hub for Nvidia chips that U.S. officials say have reached China. The U.S. has imposed export restrictions on Nvidia's most cutting-edge AI chips to China since 2022 to curb Beijing's surging AI development. Nvidia's revenue linked to Singapore rose to 22% in the fiscal quarter ending July 2025, up from 8% in 2023, with the country's trade ministry estimating chips physically delivered there accounted for less than 1% of the chipmaker's revenue. Experts have pointed to gaps in enforcement of U.S. export restrictions and Singapore's corporate system that make it hard to trace where advanced Nvidia chips ultimately end up. Nvidia chips can be legally sold to customers in other countries, such as Malaysia or Singapore, and then illicitly resold or re-exported to China. Chinese companies can also legally gain remote access to the most advanced AI chips hosted in data centers outside China rather than buying the hardware directly. Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at Council on Foreign Relations and former U.S. national security official, said that Southeast Asia has become "a major hub for chip smuggling and export control circumvention," importing tens of billions of dollars' worth of AI chips per year. Singapore has stepped up efforts to police suspected chip diversion since last year, including investigations involving alleged fraud and money laundering. Authorities acknowledged the potential "blind spots between separate monitoring of trade flows and banking flows," said Alvin Camba, lead scientist and director of research at Lyvi, an Austin-based AI risk assessment firm. Correlating physical shipments with related financial transactions can be "challenging," he added. "Singapore's strong corporate secrecy regulations, which offer extensive protections for foreign investors, can also make it difficult to rapidly identify the true recipients of goods," Camba said. Those challenges can be exploited to "obfuscate financial flows and potentially circumvent global restrictions on technology transfers," he added, urging constant adaptation from regulators. Singapore said it had received limited help from U.S. authorities in its yearlong investigation. Police sought information on Super Micro Computer Inc., a U.S. server supplier relevant to the probe, but the company provided limited cooperation, according to the Thursday statement. The city-state first raised the issue with U.S. authorities in July 2025, and has repeated its request on several occasions since September last year. "Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company," it said. Police interviewed Alice Huang, a Hong Kong resident who was then Megaspeed's CEO, chairperson and a key controller, in June 2025. In February 2026, authorities concluded that there was insufficient evidence that she had committed offenses related to the declarations under investigation. She was nonetheless barred from re-entering Singapore after being found providing inaccurate information to downplay her role in Megaspeed. The country does not enforce "unilateral export controls" imposed by other countries, the ministry said in Thursday's statement, but it expects companies operating there to take foreign export rules into account in their international business activities. Megaspeed, which was spun off from a Chinese gaming company, became Nvidia's largest Southeast Asian customer in less than three years and has bought more than $4.8 billion worth of its chips since June 2024, according to The New York Times, though the company has denied any wrongdoing. Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese intelligence asset passing information to Beijing, served as managing director at Megaspeed for eight months in 2023 but has reportedly continued to play a leading role at the company. Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday, ending 33 years at the helm after revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker at the heart of the global AI boom into crisis. Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent successor. Got a confidential news tip? We want to hear from you. coreStoryFacts.text: Singapore, a hub for billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia sales each year, finds itself increasingly in the crosshairs of Washington's push to stop advanced AI chips from reaching China, as the chipmaker CEO's scandal once again thrusts the city-state into the spotlight.
Nvidia chips can be legally sold to customers in other countries, such as Malaysia or Singapore, and then illicitly resold or re-exported to China.
The alleged transactions in the broader case totaled about $390 million, prosecutors said March last year.
Singapore has faced growing international scrutiny, particularly from the U.S., over its role as a major billing and potential transit hub for Nvidia chips that U.S. officials say have reached China.

Nvidia's revenue linked to Singapore rose to 22% in the fiscal quarter ending July 2025, up from 8% in 2023, with the country's trade ministry estimating chips physically delivered there accounted for less than 1% of the chipmaker's revenue.

Megaspeed, which was spun off from a Chinese gaming company, became Nvidia's largest Southeast Asian customer in less than three years and has bought more than $4.8 billion worth of its chips since June 2024, according to The New York Times, though the company has denied any wrongdoing.
Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent successor.
A U.S. trade official in 2025 confirmed boxes of unopened Nvidia chips at a Speedmatrix data centre, raising suspicions that the equipment may have been illegally re-exported to China.
Megaspeed International, which has presented itself as an Nvidia cloud partner, has again come under scrutiny as suspicions grow that restricted Nvidia chips have entered China.

extraction.body: Singapore, a hub for billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia sales each year, finds itself increasingly in the crosshairs of Washington's push to stop advanced AI chips from reaching China, as the chipmaker CEO's scandal once again thrusts the city-state into the spotlight. The Southeast Asian nation said Thursday that it had barred Alice Huang, the businesswoman at the center of a scandal that catalyzed the end of Jensen Huang's run as Nvidia CEO, from re-entering the country. A fifth person was handed 41 charges on Friday in a Singapore fraud case involving computer servers that might have contained Nvidia chips and were exported to Malaysia. The alleged transactions in the broader case totaled about $390 million, prosecutors said March last year. The investigations into several companies and key officials, including Megaspeed International, began in February 2025 and remained ongoing as of Thursday. Authorities have been examining whether servers exported through Singapore to Malaysia without entering the domestic market were subsequently rerouted to another destination, contrary to declarations made in Singapore, the Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement late Thursday. Singapore has faced growing international scrutiny, particularly from the U.S., over its role as a major billing and potential transit hub for Nvidia chips that U.S. officials say have reached China. The U.S. has imposed export restrictions on Nvidia's most cutting-edge AI chips to China since 2022 to curb Beijing's surging AI development. Nvidia's revenue linked to Singapore rose to 22% in the fiscal quarter ending July 2025, up from 8% in 2023, with the country's trade ministry estimating chips physically delivered there accounted for less than 1% of the chipmaker's revenue. Experts have pointed to gaps in enforcement of U.S. export restrictions and Singapore's corporate system that make it hard to trace where advanced Nvidia chips ultimately end up. Nvidia chips can be legally sold to customers in other countries, such as Malaysia or Singapore, and then illicitly resold or re-exported to China. Chinese companies can also legally gain remote access to the most advanced AI chips hosted in data centers outside China rather than buying the hardware directly. Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at Council on Foreign Relations and former U.S. national security official, said that Southeast Asia has become "a major hub for chip smuggling and export control circumvention," importing tens of billions of dollars' worth of AI chips per year. Singapore has stepped up efforts to police suspected chip diversion since last year, including investigations involving alleged fraud and money laundering. Authorities acknowledged the potential "blind spots between separate monitoring of trade flows and banking flows," said Alvin Camba, lead scientist and director of research at Lyvi, an Austin-based AI risk assessment firm. Correlating physical shipments with related financial transactions can be "challenging," he added. "Singapore's strong corporate secrecy regulations, which offer extensive protections for foreign investors, can also make it difficult to rapidly identify the true recipients of goods," Camba said. Those challenges can be exploited to "obfuscate financial flows and potentially circumvent global restrictions on technology transfers," he added, urging constant adaptation from regulators. Singapore said it had received limited help from U.S. authorities in its yearlong investigation. Police sought information on Super Micro Computer Inc., a U.S. server supplier relevant to the probe, but the company provided limited cooperation, according to the Thursday statement. The city-state first raised the issue with U.S. authorities in July 2025, and has repeated its request on several occasions since September last year. "Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company," it said. Police interviewed Alice Huang, a Hong Kong resident who was then Megaspeed's CEO, chairperson and a key controller, in June 2025. In February 2026, authorities concluded that there was insufficient evidence that she had committed offenses related to the declarations under investigation. She was nonetheless barred from re-entering Singapore after being found providing inaccurate information to downplay her role in Megaspeed. The country does not enforce "unilateral export controls" imposed by other countries, the ministry said in Thursday's statement, but it expects companies operating there to take foreign export rules into account in their international business activities. Megaspeed, which was spun off from a Chinese gaming company, became Nvidia's largest Southeast Asian customer in less than three years and has bought more than $4.8 billion worth of its chips since June 2024, according to The New York Times, though the company has denied any wrongdoing. Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese intelligence asset passing information to Beijing, served as managing director at Megaspeed for eight months in 2023 but has reportedly continued to play a leading role at the company. Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday, ending 33 years at the helm after revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker at the heart of the global AI boom into crisis. Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent successor. Got a confidential news tip? We want to hear from you. U.S. export controls were designed to slow China’s AI development.

ByteDance building capacity offshore only deepens that relationship.

passages: Smaller AI labs are also considering similar moves, including through providers in Southeast Asia.The concern centres on the Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, a US bill that would give the Commerce Department authority to regulate remote, cloud-based access to restricted technology.Washington already restricts exporting Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips to CHina over national security concerns.

These have been tightened several times in the last couple of years to keep China from gaining access to cutting-edge computing power that could support advanced AI and military applications.It also sets a murky stage for US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping's meeting next week, adding yet another issue to the agenda as the two countries remain locked in a broader technology and trade rivalry.China is willing to work on "important common understandings reached between the two presidents, and build a constructive relationship," the spokesperson said.Beijing has earlier rejected the “so-called Chinese spy allegation,” saying it is unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against China.Nvidia has said its board has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

sources.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
passages: U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security.
This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday.

Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him.

Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. Nvidia confirmed in an SEC filing on Thursday that the board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang. Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993. Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26. “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.” The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed. After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO. According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year. Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed . The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum. Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported . The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips. Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang. In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported. On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO. “I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said. When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia , Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.” Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife. An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary. “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.” U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times. Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo. Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service. Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born. Nvidia’s board launched an independent probe after a classified U.S. memo alleged Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to target Jensen Huang Nvidia makes the processors that power large-scale artificial intelligence systems. U.S. export controls restrict the most advanced of those chips from reaching China, a country competing directly with the United States in AI development. Those rules reflect bipartisan concern that advanced AI processors could accelerate China’s military and surveillance capabilities, which is what transforms the following sequence of events from a corporate personnel matter into a national-security concern. Jensen Huang leads Nvidia; Alice Huang ran operations at a firm built on Nvidia’s technology. Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it since. Alice Huang , also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen and former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data-center company that rents computing capacity built on Nvidia processors. She is not related to Jensen Huang. Media accounts placed the pair together in Taiwan multiple times before any investigation became public. During 2024 and into 2025 , media reports said Jensen Huang and Alice Huang were photographed or observed socializing in Taiwan, where Jensen Huang was born. Those encounters later became relevant to intelligence reporting about the alleged operation, according to the cited reporting. No public statement about the relationship was identified in that reporting from either Nvidia or U.S. officials at the time. U.S. and Singapore authorities opened parallel inquiries into whether Nvidia chips reached China through a third-party operator. In October 2025 , U.S. and Singapore authorities reportedly examined whether Megaspeed had helped Chinese firms, including Alibaba, obtain Nvidia processors in potential violation of U.S. export restrictions. Export controls are rules that restrict the sale of certain advanced technology to designated countries, entities, or uses, sometimes requiring government licensing. Officials also questioned the disposition of Nvidia equipment observed at a Malaysian facility, according to the supplied reporting, as AI is making enforcement of such controls increasingly complex. The president learned of the intelligence months before it became public. The New York Times reported that in late 2025, President Trump was informed about intelligence concerning Alice Huang’s alleged activities and her relationship with Jensen Huang. No publicly announced action was identified in the cited reporting at that time. The briefing was not disclosed until reporting on the broader story emerged in late October 2026. U.S. officials reportedly concluded Alice Huang was working for Chinese intelligence, though that assessment has not been independently verified. In spring 2026 , U.S. officials reportedly circulated a classified memo alleging that Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security , the country’s primary civilian intelligence agency. The memo allegedly stated she had been recruited to gather information about Jensen Huang . It also alleged she was tasked with influencing Nvidia’s commercial position on advanced chip sales to China. This is an intelligence assessment reported by news organizations citing unnamed officials; it is not an established legal or investigative finding. Such government restrictions on technology access echo broader debates over how authorities worldwide handle sensitive data, as seen when Europe restricts major cloud providers from handling sensitive public-sector information. A New York Times report in October 2026 brought the relationship and the investigation into public view. On October 29, 2026 , the New York Times disclosed that U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year and that she had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Nvidia responded by characterizing Jensen Huang’s interactions with her as ordinary customer-related contact. A rapid sequence of corporate and political responses followed that disclosure. Three House committee chairmen asked Jensen Huang to appear before a closed-door session. The chairmen of the House Select Committee on China, the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and the House Intelligence Committee formally requested a closed-door briefing from Jensen Huang, with the request reported around November 5, 2026. The letter cited concerns about Chinese access to sensitive U.S. technology and possible infiltration of American technology companies. No public response from Huang or Nvidia was identified in the cited reporting at that time. The CEO issued a public apology on November 8 without naming Alice Huang. On November 8, 2026 , Jensen Huang publicly acknowledged that he had been unfaithful, apologizing to his wife, children, Nvidia employees, and the company. He also withdrew from planned appearances at the ElevenLabs Summit and the Anthropic CEO Forum. The board acted the following day, saying it had no immediate evidence of compromised secrets. Trump later added that Huang had told him he did not know Alice Huang was allegedly a spy. Beijing’s Foreign Ministry called the espionage claim “groundless speculation.” On November 10, 2026 , China’s Foreign Ministry characterized the allegation that Alice Huang was working for Chinese intelligence as a smear and rejected it as unsubstantiated. Corporate records, as reported by media, separately identified her as a Megaspeed director from March to November 2023. The supplied reporting does not identify her current status or whereabouts. The investigation is ongoing, and several core questions have no public answers yet. Public reporting has not established what information Alice Huang allegedly obtained, whether any Nvidia proprietary information was transferred, or whether export-control violations involving Megaspeed occurred. Nvidia’s independent board investigation has not released findings. extraction.body: WASHINGTON (TNND) — In a stunning development, Nvidia announced Thursday that Jensen Huang had resigned from the company he helped found in 1993. The resignation followed revelations that Huang reportedly had affairs with two women: an executive who reported to him and a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. Lawmakers on Capitol Hill reacted swiftly. Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said, “It was the right thing to do. Now we have to get to the bottom of whether America's national security has been compromised.” House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-LA, called it “a big and shocking development,” adding, “That's a very important company not only in the U.S. economy but for national security purposes.” Although the affair became public this week, the timeline of events described in published reports stretches back years. According to The Wall Street Journal, in 2023 Alice Huang created 'Megaspeed,' a company seeking to build data centers in Asia using Nvidia chips. In June 2024, Alice and Jensen Huang were photographed together in Taiwan, and again in May 2025. Later that year, The New York Times reported that federal investigators were looking into 'Megaspeed,' the potential export of chips to China, and the connection between the two. In December, President Trump agreed to let Nvidia export a less powerful chip to China in exchange for 25% of the sales going to the federal government. By 2026, suspicion was reportedly growing. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was reportedly supervising the drafting of a classified memo warning of a personal relationship between the two. The report of the memo came shortly before Huang was a last-minute addition to Trump’s China trip in May, which included various other tech giants. This week, Huang confirmed the extramarital relationship for the first time, writing, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children.” Nvidia stock continued to tumble in the aftermath of the news and Huang’s resignation. Yahoo Finance reported the company had shed $490 billion in market value by the end of trading Thursday. Nvidia’s board of directors also said Thursday that the company’s current executive vice president and CFO has agreed to serve as interim CEO, and that the board will search for Huang’s replacement, considering both internal and external candidates.
passages: WASHINGTON (TNND) — In a stunning development, Nvidia announced Thursday that Jensen Huang had resigned from the company he helped found in 1993. The resignation followed revelations that Huang reportedly had affairs with two women: an executive who reported to him and a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.

Lawmakers on Capitol Hill reacted swiftly. Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said, “It was the right thing to do. Now we have to get to the bottom of whether America's national security has been compromised.” House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-LA, called it “a big and shocking development,” adding, “That's a very important company not only in the U.S. economy but for national security purposes.”

Although the affair became public this week, the timeline of events described in published reports stretches back years. According to The Wall Street Journal, in 2023 Alice Huang created 'Megaspeed,' a company seeking to build data centers in Asia using Nvidia chips. In June 2024, Alice and Jensen Huang were photographed together in Taiwan, and again in May 2025.

Later that year, The New York Times reported that federal investigators were looking into 'Megaspeed,' the potential export of chips to China, and the connection between the two. In December, President Trump agreed to let Nvidia export a less powerful chip to China in exchange for 25% of the sales going to the federal government.

By 2026, suspicion was reportedly growing. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was reportedly supervising the drafting of a classified memo warning of a personal relationship between the two. The report of the memo came shortly before Huang was a last-minute addition to Trump’s China trip in May, which included various other tech giants.
This week, Huang confirmed the extramarital relationship for the first time, writing, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children.”
Nvidia stock continued to tumble in the aftermath of the news and Huang’s resignation. Yahoo Finance reported the company had shed $490 billion in market value by the end of trading Thursday.

Nvidia’s board of directors also said Thursday that the company’s current executive vice president and CFO has agreed to serve as interim CEO, and that the board will search for Huang’s replacement, considering both internal and external candidates.

This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday.

Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him.
Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report.
Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said .
The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties.

extraction.body: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. Nvidia confirmed in an SEC filing on Thursday that the board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang. Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993. Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26. “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.” The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed. After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO. According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year. Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed . The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum. Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported . The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips. Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang. In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported. On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO. “I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said. When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia , Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.” Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife. An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary. “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.” U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times. Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo. Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service. Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born. These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. The resignation followed revelations that Huang reportedly had affairs with two women: an executive who reported to him and a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. Later that year, The New York Times reported that federal investigators were looking into 'Megaspeed,' the potential export of chips to China, and the connection between the two. Nvidia’s board of directors also said Thursday that the company’s current executive vice president and CFO has agreed to serve as interim CEO, and that the board will search for Huang’s replacement, considering both internal and external candidates.

extraction.body: Microsoft Outlook continues to be unavailable for people, businesses, and public services across the globe, leaving people unable to access their email, either through the web or apps. Reports around the issue starting rolling in at around 1PM ET on Thursday, with Microsoft since confirming that the outage is impacting Microsoft 365 features that interact with Exchange Online and email services, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Copilot AI, and other 365 business services. When the outage issues were first identified on Thursday, Microsoft acknowledged from its Microsoft 365 Status account that “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” Microsoft has gone through several variations of update notes since then, providing suprisingly detailed bulletins about the issues and its attempts to fix them. While Microsoft said it initially had problems rebooting servers and being able to monitor their health, its last few updates say that recovery efforts are going well: > We’re seeing early stabilization and capacity improvements as recovery actions continue. To help preserve delayed mail during this event, we’ve extended email timeout to 48 hours. > Recovery actions are ongoing across affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure and progressing in phases. We’re seeing incremental improvement in several workloads, but service health remains variable and capacity has not yet fully returned to baseline. > We’ve made additional progress toward recovery, with actions now completed across portions of affected infrastructure and traffic being gradually restored. We’re seeing improvements in key scenarios, including mailbox access and delayed email processing, though some intermittent issues may continue. Our focus is extending these recovery actions across remaining affected infrastructure while continuing stabilization and adding capacity to improve consistency. There’s still no ETA for full restoration, but we will continue to monitor this ongoing outage. Update, November 13th: Updated with the latest information from Microsoft.

sources.title: Microsoft reports ‘encouraging recovery progress’ in global outage that has impacted millions - CNN
passages: • Making headway: Microsoft said it is seeing “encouraging recovery progress” in an hourslong outage that has affected millions around the world.
The tech giant warns some users may still “experience intermittent issues.”
“The idea that after the CrowdStrike outage and after other outages that we’ve seen, that a company like Microsoft could have an outage that would be global in nature is unthinkable.”
Memes and jokes abounded online as the global outage of Microsoft’s Outlook emails and Teams meeting platform crossed the 12-hour mark.
US lawmakers: The US House of Representatives said the outage impacted its users and its engineers were working with Microsoft, according to Reuters .
Some congressional staffers expressed frustration on X.
“Shall we start conducting all official business via DM?” said Sharon Eliza Nichols, communications director for Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton.
Microsoft said that it would extend its email timeout window to 48 hours “to help protect delayed messages while service recovery continues,” according to an update posted at around 4:15 a.m.
• What’s been impacted: The outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life .
AI companies said they were facing issues as well.
Banks, governments, health services, railways and courts all reported disruptions across Microsoft products .
The outage was not caused by a cybersecurity breach , the company has said.
Claude creator Anthropic said shortly after 6 a.m.
ET that a fix had been deployed and it was “monitoring for recovery.”
Microsoft’s outage reports “reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour,” according to Downdetector, a website that tracks cyber outages.
Microsoft executivesCharles Lamanna said in the early hours of Friday that there is currently no indication that the outage is the result “of malicious or cyber activity.”
Teams: Anything that has already been scheduled and requires Teams — Microsoft’s communications platform — to connect with a user’s calendar is likely impacted.
But if users are simply just joining a call or exchanging messages, that is still working.
A user on X said : “whoever is troubleshooting and working on the Microsoft outage for outlook and teams…. take your time.”
At first, Microsoft said the connection issues were happening “in the Americas,” but over time it became clear the troubles were global.
Copilot: Users may also be unable to load chats with or receive responses from Microsoft’s AI tool.
Copilot also cannot access the data it normally draws from, like emails, files and calendars.
CNN’s Nina Avramova contributed to this report.
Email down : Outlook remains down and users are also having trouble accessing their Exchange Online mailboxes.

But if users are simply just joining a call or exchanging messages, that is still working. Word/Excel/Powerpoint: The basic functions of these apps are still working. However, other functions may be impacted, like if users are trying to print documents over the cloud or share documents with Sharepoint. Users may also not be able to view their most recently used files. CNN’s Nina Avramova contributed to this report. The email timeout window is the maximum amount of time that a mail server or email client such as Outlook will spend waiting to receive an email before returning an error. Microsoft said recovery efforts are ongoing and that it’s seeing “early signs of stabilization,” though service capacity has not returned to normal. Memes and jokes abounded online as the global outage of Microsoft’s Outlook emails and Teams meeting platform crossed the 12-hour mark. Microsoft’s outage reports “reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour,” according to Downdetector, a website that tracks cyber outages. “Reports did not stay in the Americas. They jumped tenfold in the UK at 17:43 (12:43 PM ET) , in India at 23:21 local time and in New Zealand at 06:55 local time. Between 17:00 and 18:55 UTC, nearly 3 in 10 reports came from outside the US,” Downdetector wrote on X . “If one of those firms suffers a major outage, it has the potential to dramatically reduce business productivity globally during the outage time,” Computing Professor Toby Murray, of Australia’s University of Melbourne, said. Murray added that the outage affecting Outlook and other major services like Microsoft Teams is “incredibly widespread, and its ramifications extend well beyond being able to send and receive work emails,” making it difficult for businesses to operate. “Outlook and Teams are critical global business infrastructure. extraction.body: More than 130,000 incident reports were submitted to Downdetector during the outage , though that figure measures submitted reports rather than a confirmed count of distinct affected users. The scale of those reports still signals a substantial network disruption hitting Outlook and Exchange Online users in multiple regions at once. Exchange Online mailboxes are the central reported failure point, with symptoms varying by connection method and tenant configuration. Users are reporting inability to open Outlook, send or receive email, or hold a stable connection to their mailbox. Specific symptoms vary depending on how a user connects and how their organization's tenant is configured. Microsoft has identified potential impact beyond email, though the full scope of affected services remains under evaluation. Microsoft has flagged possible impact on Teams, SharePoint Online, Copilot 365, and Defender XDR . Microsoft 365 services separately confirmed it resolved an earlier Teams disruption affecting users in North America, but broader Microsoft 365 connectivity problems remain active and are separate from that resolved incident. Microsoft attributes the connectivity errors to elevated infrastructure load across multiple regions, though the investigation is ongoing. Microsoft's stated explanation points to elevated infrastructure load across multiple regions, which the company believes is contributing to connectivity errors. This is an infrastructure capacity or traffic-management problem currently under investigation. No available reporting establishes malicious activity as the cause. Microsoft is restarting and repairing affected infrastructure while also evaluating whether rerouting traffic could accelerate recovery. The company says it is restarting and repairing affected infrastructure to restore capacity. Microsoft is also evaluating whether traffic can be redirected to alternate infrastructure to speed the recovery process. Organizations dependent on Microsoft 365 may see interruptions across email, calendar, authentication, and collaboration tools, depending on how their tenant is affected. If your organization's tenant is affected, you may experience interruptions across email workflows, calendar access, authentication processes, and collaboration tools. The severity will vary depending on your tenant configuration and which Microsoft 365 services your teams rely on. The Microsoft 365 admin center is the authoritative source for tenant-specific incident details and mitigation updates. Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center and navigate to Health, then Service health, to review active incidents affecting Exchange Online and related services. Hold off on resetting passwords or rebuilding Outlook profiles until you have confirmed what Microsoft's incident updates say. First, verify what the incident details say about your specific tenant. The admin center provides tenant-specific detail that public status pages may not reflect. For broader guidance on computer problems and connectivity troubleshooting, IT teams can consult additional resources while awaiting Microsoft's resolution. Key questions about Microsoft's recovery timeline and secondary service restoration remain unanswered. Microsoft's recovery timeline remains unclear, and it is not yet confirmed whether all flagged secondary services will fully recover alongside Exchange Online. Watch for Microsoft's post-incident review on what caused the load surge and how the company plans to prevent a repeat. The Microsoft 365 Service Health Dashboard and Microsoft's public status channels are the most authoritative real-time sources to monitor until full service is restored.

sources.title: Microsoft Outlook Still Down for Some Users as Microsoft 365 Outage Continues - ThePCEnthusiast
passages: Microsoft is still struggling to fully restore Outlook and Microsoft 365 after a widespread outage disrupted email access, business communications, and government operations worldwide.
The disruption began Thursday, November 12, and continues to affect users Friday morning despite Microsoft’s efforts to bring its servers back online.
For users wondering whether Outlook is still down, the answer depends on their region, organization, and the services they are trying to access.
Some functionality has recovered, but Microsoft has not declared the incident fully resolved.
IT administrators can also track incidents EX1550543 and MO1550821 through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center.
However, the disruption extends well beyond email.
Not every Microsoft 365 service is completely offline.
Microsoft says functions that do not depend on the affected Exchange Online infrastructure may continue working normally.
The outage primarily affects Exchange Online, the email infrastructure behind many business and enterprise Outlook accounts.
Users have reported being unable to open their inboxes, send or receive messages, or connect through Outlook’s web, desktop, and mobile applications.
Microsoft also confirmed that it has found no evidence of malicious activity associated with the outage.
A final root cause has not been established, and a post-incident report will be released after the disruption is resolved.
At 6:01 AM EST on November 13, Microsoft reported that recovery actions had been completed across portions of its Asia-Pacific infrastructure.
Mailbox access and delayed email processing were improving, but intermittent issues remained.
Microsoft has also extended its email timeout window to 48 hours to help preserve delayed messages while outstanding email queues are processed.
This is a recovery measure, not an indication that the outage will last another 48 hours.
In its latest verified update, Microsoft confirmed that recovery efforts remain underway.
The company has not provided an estimated time for full restoration.
However, some servers that appeared healthy after restarting became unresponsive again when traffic returned, complicating recovery.
Further investigation found that a process responsible for establishing secure connections was becoming overwhelmed.
Microsoft has since applied an authentication and routing configuration patch, restarted affected infrastructure, and introduced traffic-management measures to improve stability.
The scale of the outage became apparent Thursday afternoon when Downdetector recorded nearly 130,000 reports of Outlook problems shortly after 1 PM EST.

coreStoryFacts.text: Microsoft Outlook continues to be unavailable for people, businesses, and public services across the globe, leaving people unable to access their email, either through the web or apps.
• Making headway: Microsoft said it is seeing “encouraging recovery progress” in an hourslong outage that has affected millions around the world.
The tech giant warns some users may still “experience intermittent issues.”
“The idea that after the CrowdStrike outage and after other outages that we’ve seen, that a company like Microsoft could have an outage that would be global in nature is unthinkable.”
Memes and jokes abounded online as the global outage of Microsoft’s Outlook emails and Teams meeting platform crossed the 12-hour mark.
US lawmakers: The US House of Representatives said the outage impacted its users and its engineers were working with Microsoft, according to Reuters .
Some congressional staffers expressed frustration on X.
“Shall we start conducting all official business via DM?” said Sharon Eliza Nichols, communications director for Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton.
Microsoft said that it would extend its email timeout window to 48 hours “to help protect delayed messages while service recovery continues,” according to an update posted at around 4:15 a.m.
• What’s been impacted: The outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life .
AI companies said they were facing issues as well.
Banks, governments, health services, railways and courts all reported disruptions across Microsoft products .
The outage was not caused by a cybersecurity breach , the company has said.
Claude creator Anthropic said shortly after 6 a.m.
ET that a fix had been deployed and it was “monitoring for recovery.”
Microsoft’s outage reports “reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour,” according to Downdetector, a website that tracks cyber outages.
Microsoft executivesCharles Lamanna said in the early hours of Friday that there is currently no indication that the outage is the result “of malicious or cyber activity.”
Teams: Anything that has already been scheduled and requires Teams — Microsoft’s communications platform — to connect with a user’s calendar is likely impacted.
But if users are simply just joining a call or exchanging messages, that is still working.
A user on X said : “whoever is troubleshooting and working on the Microsoft outage for outlook and teams…. take your time.”
At first, Microsoft said the connection issues were happening “in the Americas,” but over time it became clear the troubles were global.
Copilot: Users may also be unable to load chats with or receive responses from Microsoft’s AI tool.
Copilot also cannot access the data it normally draws from, like emails, files and calendars.
More than 130,000 incident reports were submitted to Downdetector during the outage , though that figure measures submitted reports rather than a confirmed count of distinct affected users.

extraction.body: Microsoft Outlook continues to be unavailable for people, businesses, and public services across the globe, leaving people unable to access their email, either through the web or apps. Reports around the issue starting rolling in at around 1PM ET on Thursday, with Microsoft since confirming that the outage is impacting Microsoft 365 features that interact with Exchange Online and email services, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Copilot AI, and other 365 business services. When the outage issues were first identified on Thursday, Microsoft acknowledged from its Microsoft 365 Status account that “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” Microsoft has gone through several variations of update notes since then, providing suprisingly detailed bulletins about the issues and its attempts to fix them. While Microsoft said it initially had problems rebooting servers and being able to monitor their health, its last few updates say that recovery efforts are going well: > We’re seeing early stabilization and capacity improvements as recovery actions continue. To help preserve delayed mail during this event, we’ve extended email timeout to 48 hours. > Recovery actions are ongoing across affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure and progressing in phases. We’re seeing incremental improvement in several workloads, but service health remains variable and capacity has not yet fully returned to baseline. > We’ve made additional progress toward recovery, with actions now completed across portions of affected infrastructure and traffic being gradually restored. We’re seeing improvements in key scenarios, including mailbox access and delayed email processing, though some intermittent issues may continue. Our focus is extending these recovery actions across remaining affected infrastructure while continuing stabilization and adding capacity to improve consistency. There’s still no ETA for full restoration, but we will continue to monitor this ongoing outage. Update, November 13th: Updated with the latest information from Microsoft.

passages: Microsoft is still struggling to fully restore Outlook and Microsoft 365 after a widespread outage disrupted email access, business communications, and government operations worldwide.
The disruption began Thursday, November 12, and continues to affect users Friday morning despite Microsoft’s efforts to bring its servers back online.
For users wondering whether Outlook is still down, the answer depends on their region, organization, and the services they are trying to access.
Some functionality has recovered, but Microsoft has not declared the incident fully resolved.
IT administrators can also track incidents EX1550543 and MO1550821 through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center.
However, the disruption extends well beyond email.
Not every Microsoft 365 service is completely offline.
Microsoft says functions that do not depend on the affected Exchange Online infrastructure may continue working normally.
The outage primarily affects Exchange Online, the email infrastructure behind many business and enterprise Outlook accounts.
Users have reported being unable to open their inboxes, send or receive messages, or connect through Outlook’s web, desktop, and mobile applications.
Microsoft also confirmed that it has found no evidence of malicious activity associated with the outage.
A final root cause has not been established, and a post-incident report will be released after the disruption is resolved.
At 6:01 AM EST on November 13, Microsoft reported that recovery actions had been completed across portions of its Asia-Pacific infrastructure.
Mailbox access and delayed email processing were improving, but intermittent issues remained.
Microsoft has also extended its email timeout window to 48 hours to help preserve delayed messages while outstanding email queues are processed.
This is a recovery measure, not an indication that the outage will last another 48 hours.
In its latest verified update, Microsoft confirmed that recovery efforts remain underway.
The company has not provided an estimated time for full restoration.
However, some servers that appeared healthy after restarting became unresponsive again when traffic returned, complicating recovery.
Further investigation found that a process responsible for establishing secure connections was becoming overwhelmed.
Microsoft has since applied an authentication and routing configuration patch, restarted affected infrastructure, and introduced traffic-management measures to improve stability.
The scale of the outage became apparent Thursday afternoon when Downdetector recorded nearly 130,000 reports of Outlook problems shortly after 1 PM EST.

The Times had reported a relationship with a vice president, and Huang has agreed to testify to Congress about Alice Huang, whom US intelligence suspects of spying for China. Hours after stepping down as chief executive of Nvidia, co-founder Jensen Huang has been linked to a third extramarital relationship involving a second employee at the semiconductor giant, according to a report by Reuters, quoted by The New York Post. Citing two sources familiar with the previously undisclosed romance, the outlet noted that the latest woman—whose identity remains unconfirmed and who could not be reached for comment—joins a growing scandal surrounding the 63-year-old executive, who has been married to his wife, Lori, for over four decades. Huang resigned on Thursday following earlier disclosures of affairs with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s 48-year-old vice president of health care, and Alice Huang, a Chinese business executive suspected by U.S. intelligence officials of conducting espionage for Beijing. Reporting from the New York Times previously detailed how Powell, who has been with the chipmaker since 2008 and reported directly to the CEO, was spotted sharing affectionate moments with Huang at a hotel during Nvidia’s March developer conference in San Jose, California—an incident reportedly filmed by a bystander who was subsequently stopped by Huang’s security team and presented with a nondisclosure agreement. Meanwhile, Huang’s involvement with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le and a former managing director at Singapore-based cloud firm Megaspeed International, has triggered national security scrutiny over assessments that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited her to gather intelligence on the billionaire founder. Although Beijing has denied the spying claims and no evidence indicates Huang knowingly aided foreign intelligence, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast confirmed Thursday that Huang has agreed to testify before Congress after Republican lawmakers threatened a subpoena, leaving interim CEO Colette Kress to guide the company as directors search for a permanent replacement. extraction.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had third extramarital affair, Reuters reports Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second company employee, in addition to two previously reported extramarital affairs, Reuters reported on November 12, citing two people familiar with the matter. The revelation came hours after Huang resigned from the chipmaking giant he had led for 33 years, amid a scandal involving a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of working for China. Reuters did not identify the newly reported employee and said attempts to contact her had been unsuccessful. The two previously reported relationships involved Alice Huang, also known as Huang Li, whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese intelligence operative, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. Alice Huang, a Chinese national associated with Singapore-based technology company Megaspeed, has reportedly come under scrutiny over possible connections to China's Ministry of State Security. The allegations of espionage have not been publicly proven. Huang, 63, acknowledged having an extramarital affair in a November 8 statement and apologized for hurting his wife and children. He did not identify the woman involved. Earlier this month, Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation, assisted by outside legal counsel, into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company previously said it had no reason to believe corporate secrets or national security had been compromised. Nvidia declined to comment on Reuters' latest findings. Huang, Powell and a representative of Nvidia's board did not respond to requests for comment, while Alice Huang could not be reached. Following Huang's resignation, Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent replacement. Nvidia shares fell 5.5% on November 12 and have lost more than 30% of their value since an early October peak. Huang's departure raises questions about the future leadership of one of the world's most influential artificial intelligence companies, whose chips and investments have played a central role in the industry's expansion.

passages: New Delhi: Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia has not put an end to the scandal that engulfed the chipmaker’s former chief executive.

A day after his resignation following reports of two extramarital relationships, a new Reuters investigation has revealed that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, taking the number of reported relationships involving the 63-year-old to at least three.
Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter, reported that the second employee involved in the newly reported relationship had not been identified.
Nvidia declined to comment, while Huang, Powell and representatives of the company’s board did not respond to requests for comment.
The board had expressed confidence in him at the time.

One was with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, who has been suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence.
The other was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who worked directly under Huang.
Following his resignation, Nvidia appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor.
The leadership change comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia, whose chips have become central to the global artificial intelligence boom and the technological competition between the US and China.

passages: New Delhi: Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia has not put an end to the scandal that engulfed the chipmaker’s former chief executive.

A day after his resignation following reports of two extramarital relationships, a new Reuters investigation has revealed that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, taking the number of reported relationships involving the 63-year-old to at least three.
Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter, reported that the second employee involved in the newly reported relationship had not been identified.
Nvidia declined to comment, while Huang, Powell and representatives of the company’s board did not respond to requests for comment.
The board had expressed confidence in him at the time.

One was with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, who has been suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence.
The other was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who worked directly under Huang.
Following his resignation, Nvidia appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor.
The leadership change comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia, whose chips have become central to the global artificial intelligence boom and the technological competition between the US and China.
In 2017, Shekhar Gupta started ThePrint with a simple belief: Indian readers want journalism that asks why and what next, not just what.
And that enough of them would be willing to pay for good journalism.

(NVDA), weighed on the asset. BTC prices slumped nearly 7% over the past day, falling to $68,529.96 at the time of writing. Meanwhile, Ethereum (ETH) prices slipped to $1,912.54. See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox According to market commentator The Kobeissi Letter, the selling pressure led to a loss of about $150 billion in crypto markets over 48 hours. Although Bitcoin is falling to its lowest level in months, some experts believe that now is a good time to enter. Crypto analyst Michaël van de Poppe said in a post on X that he has been buying BTC, outlining five reasons for his move. He noted that the "terrible sentiment" around the underlying asset means it is hard for prices to keep declining, adding that while there have been multiple events for the asset price to crash, it hasn't yet and markets are simply witnessing a 20% correction. He also pointed out that this is a support area, "just barely beneath the 200-Day MA and ideal for liquidity." The analyst said that Bitcoin had already bottomed on the Friday prior to the SpaceX IPO and that he "wouldn't be surprised" if the present scenario was at the same cadence. "Fifthly: Nasdaq is already up a lot, meaning that there's a gap between Bitcoin and the Nasdaq. It doesn't take long for this gap to close, which is why I've been buying Bitcoin today," he said. Meanwhile, Anthony Pompliano, Founder and CEO of Professional Capital Management, said in a post on X, "Bitcoin is falling to prices we haven't seen since…..3 months ago. Everyone relax, so you can realize that AI and bitcoin are one big trade now." However, long-time crypto critic Peter Schiff is not convinced. In a post on X, he implored investors to think about how Bitcoin has been trading relative to 2021. "Think about this, HOLDers. Bitcoin just traded at a lower price than it traded in November 2021. How many of you who owned Bitcoin back then expected it to be below the Nov. 2021 high more than five years later? Bitcoin is in a long-term bear market. The long-term trend is down," he argued. Rich Rosenblum, co-founder of crypto market maker GSR, told Bloomberg that the volatility in the AI trade and continued U.S. dollar strength have impacted some long Bitcoin positions negatively, while the red-hot inflation data and changes in Nvidia Corp.'s (NVDA) leadership amid Jensen Huang's resignation are also weighing on risk assets. Dean Chen, an analyst at crypto exchange Bitunix, also said in a note Thursday, as per Bloomberg, "Bitcoin is showing signs of a changing market structure, with selling pressure concentrated in derivatives while spot market activity remains comparatively resilient." Meanwhile, futures cumulative volume delta, a measure that tracks how aggressive buyers or sellers are in the futures market, has turned deeply negative, he noted, while adding that open interest has also declined. "Taken together, these indicators suggest that leveraged exposure is cooling, but market positioning remains mixed," Chen reportedly said. Crypto-linked equities fell alongside cryptocurrencies late Thursday. Strategy (MSTR), Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR), Strive (ASST), Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN), and Robinhood Markets Inc. (HOOD) all saw their shares decline in the overnight trade. Strategy also faces pressure after MSCI Inc. said it would remove the company from its global indexes after the Nov. 30 rebalancing, likely prompting an exodus from passive funds. Caroline Mauron, co-founder of Orbit Markets, told Bloomberg that MSCI's decision to drop Strategy, which is the largest corporate buyer of BTC, from its global equity benchmarks has also been a factor affecting the cryptocurrency. "Think about this, HOLDers. Bitcoin just traded at a lower price than it traded in November 2021. How many of you who owned Bitcoin back then expected it to be below the Nov. 2021 high more than five years later? Bitcoin is in a long-term bear market. The long-term trend is down," he argued.

Rich Rosenblum, co-founder of crypto market maker GSR, told Bloomberg that the volatility in the AI trade and continued U.S. dollar strength have impacted some long Bitcoin positions negatively, while the red-hot inflation data and changes in Nvidia Corp.'s (NVDA) leadership amid Jensen Huang's resignation are also weighing on risk assets.

Dean Chen, an analyst at crypto exchange Bitunix, also said in a note Thursday, as per Bloomberg, "Bitcoin is showing signs of a changing market structure, with selling pressure concentrated in derivatives while spot market activity remains comparatively resilient."

Meanwhile, futures cumulative volume delta, a measure that tracks how aggressive buyers or sellers are in the futures market, has turned deeply negative, he noted, while adding that open interest has also declined. "Taken together, these indicators suggest that leveraged exposure is cooling, but market positioning remains mixed," Chen reportedly said.

Crypto-linked equities fell alongside cryptocurrencies late Thursday. Strategy (MSTR), Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR), Strive (ASST), Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN), and Robinhood Markets Inc. (HOOD) all saw their shares decline in the overnight trade.
Strategy also faces pressure after MSCI Inc. said it would remove the company from its global indexes after the Nov. 30 rebalancing, likely prompting an exodus from passive funds.

Caroline Mauron, co-founder of Orbit Markets, told Bloomberg that MSCI's decision to drop Strategy, which is the largest corporate buyer of BTC, from its global equity benchmarks has also been a factor affecting the cryptocurrency.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC was 'extremely bearish' at the time of writing, while it was 'bearish' for ETH.
Sentiment around MSTR was 'extremely bearish,' while ASST, COIN, and HOOD were in 'bearish' territory. Retail sentiment around BMNR improved from 'neutral' to 'bullish' over 24 hours.
BTC has lost nearly 33% of its value in the last one year, while ETH has lost more than 45% in the same time.
